title: Pulse exhausts GraphQL budget (0/5000) while REST is 92% unused — route calls through REST fallback wrappers
body:
## Task

Optimize pulse GraphQL API budget consumption — currently exhausts 5000/hr limit leaving REST budget (4613/5000) unused.

## Why

The pulse consistently hits the GraphQL rate limit (0/5000 remaining), causing cascading failures across all stages. 5208 rate-limit errors logged in a single pulse.log. Meanwhile, the REST API budget sits at 92% unused (4613/5000). The existing REST fallback mechanism (`t2574`) only covers calls routed through `gh_issue_list` wrapper — but most pulse stages bypass the wrapper and call `gh issue list` directly.

## Root Cause Analysis

### 1. Top API consumers bypass prefetch cache and REST fallback

| Script | `gh` call sites | Uses prefetch cache? | Uses REST fallback wrapper? |
|--------|----------------|---------------------|-----------------------------|
| `pulse-merge.sh` | 21 | No | No |
| `pulse-triage.sh` | 19 | No | No |
| `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` | 18 | No | No |
| `pulse-capacity-alloc.sh` | 15 | No | No |
| `pulse-merge-conflict.sh` | 11 | No | No |
| `pulse-simplification.sh` | 9 | No | No |
| `pulse-prefetch-fetch.sh` | 7 | Partial (is the cache) | No |
| `pulse-dispatch-core.sh` | 7 | No | No |
| `pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` | 7 | No | No |

### 2. Cycle frequency × repos × stages = budget exhaustion

- Timer interval: 120s = ~30 cycles/hour
- Repos: 3 pulse-enabled
- Stages per cycle: ~20 (each potentially calling `gh issue list` per repo)
- Estimated: 600-1200 GraphQL points/hour from deterministic stages alone
- LLM dispatch stage adds more on top

### 3. Existing mitigations are incomplete

- **REST fallback** (`t2574`): only covers `gh_issue_list`/`gh_create_issue`/`gh_create_pr` wrappers from `shared-gh-wrappers.sh`. Raw `gh issue list` calls bypass it entirely.
- **Circuit breaker** (`t2690`): pauses worker dispatch at <30% budget, but does NOT pause deterministic preflight stages which continue consuming points.

## How

Prioritized optimization plan:

### Phase 1: Route all gh calls through REST-fallback wrappers (highest ROI)
- EDIT: `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh` — replace all `gh issue list` with `gh_issue_list`, `gh pr list` with `gh_pr_list`
- EDIT: `pulse-merge.sh` — same replacement
- EDIT: `pulse-triage.sh` — same replacement  
- EDIT: `pulse-capacity-alloc.sh` — same replacement
- EDIT: `pulse-merge-conflict.sh` — same replacement
- EDIT: remaining `pulse-*.sh` scripts with direct `gh` calls
- This shifts load to the underutilized REST budget (4613/5000 available)

### Phase 2: Extend prefetch cache to downstream stages
- Reconcile stages (`close_issues_with_merged_prs`, `reconcile_stale_done_issues`, `reconcile_merged_pr_close`, `reconcile_parent_tasks`, `reconcile_labelless_aidevops_issues`) should read from `pulse-prefetch-cache.json` instead of making their own `gh issue list` calls
- The prefetch stage already collects this data — downstream stages duplicate the work

### Phase 3: Reduce cycle frequency for contributor repos
- Contributor-role repos (`role: contributor`) don't need 2-min polling
- Add per-repo `pulse_interval` override in `repos.json`; default 120s for maintainer, 300-600s for contributor

### Phase 4: Consolidate reconcile stages
- Five separate reconcile sub-stages each call `gh issue list` per repo
- Merge into one pass that fetches issues once and runs all reconcile logic against the result

## Acceptance Criteria

1. GraphQL budget stays above 50% (2500/5000) during normal operation
2. All `gh issue list`/`gh pr list` calls in `pulse-*.sh` go through `gh_issue_list`/`gh_pr_list` wrappers
3. REST fallback activates proactively (threshold: 1000 GraphQL points remaining)
4. No functional regression in pulse stages

## Evidence

```
# GraphQL exhausted, REST unused:
$ gh api rate_limit | jq '{graphql: .resources.graphql, core: .resources.core}'
{
  "graphql": { "limit": 5000, "used": 5000, "remaining": 0 },
  "core":    { "limit": 5000, "used": 387,  "remaining": 4613 }
}

# 5208 rate-limit errors:
$ grep -c 'rate limit' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log
5208

# Top offenders (from pulse.log):
$ grep -oP 'gh (issue|pr) \S+' ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -3
3573 gh issue list
 871 gh pr list
 848 gh pr <command>
```

## Children

Decomposition filed via #20633 (t2773/t2775/t2776 + existing t2772):

- #20642 — Phase 1: route `pulse-*.sh` gh reads through REST-fallback wrappers
- #20658 — Phase 2: route reconcile sub-stages through `pulse-prefetch-cache.json`
- #20660 — Phase 3: per-repo `pulse_interval` throttle for contributor-role repos
- #20661 — Phase 4: consolidate reconcile sub-stages into single-pass iterator

Child dispatch order: **Phase 1 and Phase 3 can ship in parallel** (independent of others). **Phase 2 should ship before Phase 4** — Phase 4 depends on the cache-read pattern Phase 2 establishes. This parent closes automatically once all four children merge (via `reconcile_completed_parent_tasks` in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`).

title: issue-sync.yml completion sweep: false positive on Ref-keyword PR bodies (regression of #19825)
body:
## Description

The `issue-sync.yml` workflow (GitHub Actions, commit author `GitHub Actions <actions@github.com>`) runs a task-completion sweep on PR merge that ignores the PR body's closing-keyword semantics. A PR titled `tNNN: description` with body `Ref #MMM` (planning-only reference) auto-marks `tNNN` complete in TODO.md and applies `status:done` to the linked issue — exactly the false-positive that #19825 (t2369) was filed to prevent.

## Expected Behavior

Per `templates/brief-template.md` and prior fix spec #19825:

> Parse PR body for `Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes` + map `#NNN` to task via `ref:GH#NNN` lookup. Mark ONLY those tasks complete.

PR bodies using `Ref #NNN` or `For #NNN` (planning-only keywords, per `prompts/build.txt` "Traceability") should not trigger completion.

## Reproducer

**Setup**: TODO.md has `- [ ] t267 ... ref:GH#1777 logged:2026-04-23`.

**PR #1799** merged on a managed private repo:

- Title: `t267: widen title + reconcile tier classification`
- Body: contains `Ref #1777` (no `Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`)
- Scope: 9 insertions, 9 deletions — ONLY updates the brief's title and tier classification. Does NOT implement t267's actual work (storage-policy.md reconciliation, which is explicitly `blocked-by:t265,t266`).

**Observed after merge**:

```bash
$ git log --oneline -3 -- TODO.md
7d1baa1 chore: mark t267 complete (pr:#1799 completed:2026-04-23) [skip ci]
bfe73ad t267: widen scope title + reconcile tier classification (#1799)
aa4dcb4 plan: add t265-t267 ...
```

Diff from the offending sweep commit:

```diff
-- [ ] t267 Reconcile storage-policy.md with complete storage architecture (Git + S3 + all Supabase tenants + local-only) #docs ... ref:GH#1777 logged:2026-04-23
+- [x] t267 Reconcile storage-policy.md with complete storage architecture (Git + S3 + all Supabase tenants + local-only) #docs ... ref:GH#1777 logged:2026-04-23 pr:#1799 completed:2026-04-23
```

Issue #1777 label also flipped to `status:done` in the same sweep.

**Impact**: t267's actual work (doc reconciliation blocked-by:t265,t266) is now invisible to the pulse. Pulse sees `[x]` + `status:done` → skips dispatch. Work is silently abandoned.

## Why the prior fix didn't cover this

#19825 (t2369) fixed the false-positive in `pulse-merge.sh` and (per body) `task-complete-helper.sh`. The sweep that fired on PR #1799 came from `GitHub Actions` commit author — strongly suggesting the `issue-sync.yml` workflow path, not the pulse path.

Hypothesis: the `issue-sync.yml` workflow runs its own completion routine that either (a) doesn't share the Layer 1 body-keyword check from #19825, or (b) shares it but has regressed. Would need to read the workflow to confirm — filing this without that investigation so the symptom is recorded with the reproducer.

## Proposed Fix

Audit all completion-sweep code paths (pulse-merge.sh, task-complete-helper.sh, issue-sync.yml, any companion scripts) for the Layer 1 body-keyword check from #19825. Wherever a task is marked `[x]`/`status:done` based on a merged PR:

1. Parse the PR body for `(Resolves|Closes|Fixes)\s+#([0-9]+)` (case-insensitive, word boundary).
2. For each captured `#NNN`, look up the TODO task via `ref:GH#NNN` and mark ONLY those complete.
3. Never infer completion from PR title task ID alone. A PR whose title starts with `tNNN:` but whose body lacks a closing keyword is a planning/refactor PR on that task's space, not a completion.

Regression test: `issue-sync.yml` workflow should have a unit/integration case where a PR with `t<claimed-id>:` title + `Ref #<linked-issue>` body merges, and t<claimed-id> remains `[ ]` in TODO.md.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In any repo with aidevops installed and `issue-sync.yml` workflow active.
2. Add a TODO entry `- [ ] tNNN <desc> ... ref:GH#MMM`.
3. Create an issue at `#MMM` linked to the TODO.
4. Open a PR with:
   - Title: `tNNN: <any description>`
   - Body: text containing `Ref #MMM` (no `Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`)
5. Merge the PR.
6. Observe: TODO.md line flipped to `[x]` with `pr:#<PR> completed:<date>`; issue #MMM labelled `status:done`.
7. Expected: TODO and issue should remain in their pre-merge state, since PR body did not use a closing keyword.

## Workarounds Applied

- **Manual TODO revert via bugfix PR** — created a bugfix PR that flips `[x] → [ ]` and strips the `pr:` / `completed:` fields. Requires claiming a fresh task ID, creating a worktree, writing a PR body, and waiting for auto-merge. ~5 min overhead per false positive.
- **Manual label reset** — `gh issue edit <N> --remove-label status:done --add-label status:available`. Needs to be done after the TODO revert PR merges so it's not re-flipped.
- Captured memory: `mem_20260423173129_0faf032b` (planning-commit-helper.sh silent failure) and the enrich bug filed as issue #20636 — this issue is the third distinct framework bug observed in the same session, all involving the issue-sync subsystem.

## Call-site Sweep

Needs maintainer investigation. Starting points for the worker:

```bash
rg -n 'mark.*complete|auto-complete|pr:#' .agents/scripts/ .github/workflows/
rg -n 'Resolves|Closes|Fixes' .agents/scripts/task-complete-helper.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh
git show 7d1baa1  # in the affected repo — authoritative reproducer diff
```

#19825's spec pointed at `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` and `.agents/scripts/task-complete-helper.sh`. The `issue-sync.yml` workflow-level invocation needs a fresh audit.

## Systemic Observation

This is the fifth issue-sync subsystem bug observed in a 2-hour session:

1. `planning-commit-helper.sh` silent commit failure (`log_warning: command not found`) — stored in memory only
2. `issue-sync-helper.sh enrich` unbound `_state_json` variable — filed as #20636
3. `gh` PATH shim signature-footer validator parse failure on shell variable title expansion — observed once, not yet filed
4. Origin label mutual-exclusion not enforced on issue creation (both `origin:interactive` and `origin:worker` applied to the same issue) — reconciled out-of-band, not filed
5. This one

Not requesting a sweep — each case has a narrow reproducer. But noting the cluster for maintainer awareness: a test/lint ratchet on the issue-sync subsystem may be overdue.

## Environment

- **aidevops version**: 3.8.96
- **Latest version**: 3.8.96
- **AI Assistant**: OpenCode (per diagnostics; actual runtime Claude Code — possible separate detection issue)
- **OS**: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS
- **Shell**: bash 5.2.21(1)-release
- **Working repo**: a managed private repo (main)
- **gh CLI**: gh version 2.90.0 (2026-04-16)

## Additional Context

- Prior art: #19825 (t2369) 2026-04-19 — fix(pulse): TODO auto-complete false-positive on range-syntax PR titles and For-keyword planning PRs. CLOSED. This bug is evidence the fix is incomplete.
- Sibling issue filed same session: #20636 — issue-sync-helper.sh enrich unbound variable.
- Workaround PR in the affected repo: link redacted (private repo).

title: Phase 3: refactor framework workflows to GitHub reusable-workflow pattern (eliminate drift class)
body:
## Task

Refactor aidevops's framework-owned GitHub Actions workflows into GitHub-native **reusable workflows** (`on: workflow_call:`), with downstream repos consuming them via tiny caller YAMLs. Eliminate per-repo script and workflow drift as an architectural class.

## Why

**Root cause we're correcting**: Framework logic was replicated per-repo instead of shared. Audit of 31 registered repos turned up 3 drifted `issue-sync.yml` copies at 659/681/714 lines vs canon 1331. Two of those 3 (`<webapp>`, `compressx-multisite`) are actively **failing every workflow run** because they have the workflow YAML but zero `.agents/scripts/` — the shell scripts the workflow calls don't exist. The third (`really-simple-ssl-multisite`) has drifted scripts too.

Phases 1 and 2 (#20648, #20649) patch the leak. This phase fixes the design so the leak can't reoccur.

**Architectural principle**: a framework that ships executable logic should have ONE source of truth for that logic. Downstream repos should opt in with configuration, not by cloning the implementation. Reusable workflows are GitHub's first-class mechanism for exactly this.

## How

### Design

**Current (replicated) model:**

```
aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← 1331 lines of logic
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh  ← framework shell
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh
aidevops/.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh

downstream-repo/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← copied, drifts
downstream-repo/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh  ← copied, drifts
downstream-repo/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh  ← copied, drifts
downstream-repo/.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh  ← copied, drifts
```

**New (reusable) model:**

```
aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml  ← 1331 lines, `on: workflow_call:`
aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← ~25-line caller for aidevops's own CI
aidevops/.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml  ← canonical caller template
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh  ← unchanged, framework source of truth
aidevops/.agents/scripts/issue-sync-lib.sh
aidevops/.agents/scripts/shared-constants.sh

downstream-repo/.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml  ← ~25-line caller, stable
(no .agents/scripts/ needed — fetched at runtime)
```

### Implementation steps

**Step 1 — Refactor `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` into reusable + caller:**

- NEW: `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` — contains ALL current jobs from `issue-sync.yml`, with:
  - Top-level trigger changed to `on: workflow_call:` with `inputs:` and `secrets:` declared
  - Each job's existing `if: github.event_name == '<X>'` guards kept (they reflect the caller's event, which is correct behaviour in reusable workflows)
  - A new first step in every job: `actions/checkout@v4` with `repository: marcusquinn/aidevops, path: __aidevops, ref: <version>` — fetches framework scripts at runtime so downstream repos don't need them checked in
  - Every `bash .agents/scripts/...` call rewritten to `bash __aidevops/.agents/scripts/...`
- EDIT: `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` — becomes a thin ~25-line caller that uses the reusable workflow via relative path: `uses: ./.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`. Preserves aidevops's own CI behaviour end-to-end.

**Step 2 — Create the canonical caller template:**

- NEW: `.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml` — the exact YAML downstream repos should carry. Model:

```yaml
# Managed by aidevops framework. Upstream logic: marcusquinn/aidevops.
# Do not edit — call aidevops check-workflows / sync-workflows to manage.
name: Issue Sync
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'TODO.md'
      - 'todo/PLANS.md'
      - 'todo/tasks/**'
  issues:
    types: [opened, edited, closed, reopened]
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      command:
        description: 'Sync command'
        required: true
        default: 'status'
        type: choice
        options: [status, pull, push, close, reconcile, enrich]

jobs:
  sync:
    uses: marcusquinn/aidevops/.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml@main
    secrets: inherit
    with:
      command: ${{ inputs.command || '' }}
```

- Include a commented-out pinned-version alternative at the top (`@v3.9.0` style) so users can opt into stable pinning.

**Step 3 — Integrate with `aidevops init`:**

- EDIT: `aidevops-init-lib.sh` — in `cmd_init`, add opt-in scaffolding for the caller YAML when `--features` includes `planning` (or a new `workflows` feature flag). Users can explicitly decline.
- EDIT: `.aidevops.json` feature schema — add `workflows` field alongside `planning`, `git_workflow`, etc. Default false (opt-in, not auto-added to existing repos).

**Step 4 — Documentation:**

- NEW: `.agents/reference/reusable-workflows.md` — architecture doc. Covers:
  - Why reusable workflows (this issue's Why section)
  - How the caller + reusable split works
  - Pinning strategies (`@main` vs `@vX.Y.Z` — tradeoffs and recommendation)
  - How `aidevops init`, `aidevops check-workflows`, `aidevops sync-workflows` interact with this model
  - Migration guide from old copied-workflow model
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — add a "Workflow architecture" subsection pointing at the new reference doc.
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` lines around 69-79 — update the SYNC_PAT description to reflect the reusable-workflow model (still per-repo secret, but the workflow file is no longer per-repo).

**Step 5 — Phase 1 + Phase 2 alignment:**

- Phase 1 (#20648) detector needs to know that "canonical downstream state" = the caller template, NOT the full 1331-line workflow. Update its manifest.
- Phase 2 (#20649) resync action becomes "install caller template", which effectively migrates any drifted full-copy repo to the caller pattern. This replaces Phase 2's originally-scoped "cp to canon" action — it's actually a better Phase 2.

**Step 6 — Tests:**

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-reusable-workflow-caller.sh` — validates the caller template is syntactically correct and references a real aidevops workflow.
- EXTEND: any existing CI that validates workflow YAML should cover the new reusable workflow + caller.

### Decisions this issue resolves

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Where does logic live? | Reusable workflow in aidevops | Single source of truth |
| How are scripts loaded? | Runtime `actions/checkout` of aidevops | Eliminates script drift as a class |
| Caller pinning strategy | Default `@main`, document `@vX.Y.Z` | Auto-update for power users, pinning available for stability |
| Downstream `.agents/scripts/` | Can be removed | No longer needed by the workflow |
| Secret handling | `secrets: inherit` in caller | SYNC_PAT still per-repo, but workflow code doesn't care |
| aidevops's own use | Thin caller pointing at reusable via relative path | Same pattern as downstream, single architecture |

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|

| `@main` pinning exposes downstream to breaking changes | Caller template header documents `@vX.Y.Z` pinning option; aidevops keeps breaking changes behind feature flags |
| Reusable workflow can't see caller's `.agents/scripts/` customisations | Intentional — customisations should be upstreamed, not repo-forked |
| GitHub Actions secret `inherit` requires modern GH version | GHES 3.7+ and all GitHub.com — no issue in practice |

## Acceptance

1. `.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml` exists, has `on: workflow_call:`, and contains the 4 jobs currently in `issue-sync.yml`.
2. `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` becomes a thin caller (`< 50 lines`) that invokes the reusable workflow via `uses: ./.github/workflows/issue-sync-reusable.yml`.
3. `.github/workflows/templates/issue-sync-caller.yml` exists and is copy-pasteable into any downstream repo.
4. aidevops's own `issue-sync` behaviour on CI is preserved end-to-end — verified by at least one full run on a PR that touches `TODO.md`.

The `gh api` call for comments lacks the `--paginate` flag. By default, the GitHub API returns only the first 30 comments in ascending chronological order (oldest first). For items with more than 30 comments, this idempotency check will fail to find the circuit breaker marker in recent comments, leading to redundant label applications and duplicate comments on every subsequent `no_work` failure. existing_nmr=$(gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${issue_number}/comments" --paginate \

```suggestion
			2>/dev/null) || existing_nmr=""
```

<details>

1. When fetching a list of items from the GitHub API with the `gh` command, use the `--paginate` flag to ensure all items are retrieved, not just the first page.
2. Avoid using the word 'issue' in review comments as it is too generic and can lead to false positives by matching phrases like 'no issues found'.

title: t2799: review-bot-gate-helper: rename RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS alias and split rate-limit vs non-review pattern sets
body:
## Session Origin

Orthogonal finding surfaced during review of #20727 (migrate `review-bot-gate.yml` to reusable-workflow pattern). The SHA-pin staleness and the pattern-array semantic mismatch both touch the same helper but are independent fixes.

**Blocked by #20727** — that migration rewrites the workflow that sources this helper. Merge #20727 first to avoid conflicts on the same file set.

## What

Clean up the misleading `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` alias in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`. After t2139 (GH#19251) expanded the array beyond rate-limit notices to include `"Review failed"`, `"Review skipped"`, and `"closed or merged during review"`, the legacy alias `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` became semantically wrong — callers that want only rate-limit patterns get non-review patterns too.

## Why

- The name `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` implies rate-limit-only but the array now contains non-rate-limit review-failure markers.
- Any downstream `custom/scripts/` caller that still references `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` for true rate-limit logic (e.g. grace-period handling via `RATE_LIMIT_GRACE_SECONDS`) is silently getting wrong behaviour — a "Review skipped" comment will trip rate-limit branches.
- Inside the framework itself there are **zero** callers of `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` (confirmed: `rg -n "RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS" .agents/ .github/` returns only the definition at line 87). Safe to retire.

## How

Two-step cleanup:

1. **Split the arrays by intent** in `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh:74-87`:
   - `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` (restored to original semantics): entries 1-6 above (`"rate limit exceeded"` through `"has exceeded the limit for..."`). Used by grace-period logic.
   - `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` (broader set, current behaviour): `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS + ("Review failed" "Review skipped" "closed or merged during review" "Auto reviews are limited")`. Used by `is_rate_limit_comment` / comment classification.
   - Build `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` as a union of `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` + the non-rate-limit entries so the two sets stay consistent.

2. **Audit the three current call sites** (`:352`, `:355`, `:626`) to confirm each is using the correct array. Line 352's comment (`# is_rate_limit_comment for accuracy — see NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS.`) suggests the classification logic wants the broader set — verify and document.

3. **Deprecate, don't delete, the alias** for one release cycle: replace `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS=("${NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS[@]}")` with a sourcing-time warning that tells downstream `custom/scripts/` callers to switch names, then remove in the next minor version. Track removal as a follow-up `ref:GH#NNN` before merging.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/review-bot-gate-helper.sh`

## Acceptance

- `RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS` contains only the 6 rate-limit entries; `NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS` contains the 10-entry union.
- All three existing call sites (`:352`, `:355`, `:626`) audited and using the array that matches their intent (documented in a comment if the choice is non-obvious).
- Grace-period logic (`RATE_LIMIT_GRACE_SECONDS`) exercised only by rate-limit matches, not by "Review skipped"-type matches.
- Deprecation warning emitted when a downstream caller references the alias (a follow-up issue filed to remove it in the next minor version).
- Existing tests pass; if any test relied on the old unified behaviour, update with a comment explaining the semantic split.

## Reference

- Review comment that surfaced this: https://github.com/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/20727#issuecomment-4314595759
- Original expansion rationale: t2139 / GH#19251 (CodeRabbit false-positive fix)

title: t2802: worktree-helper.sh add: explicitly base new branches on origin/<default> to prevent scope-leak PRs
body:
## What

`worktree-helper.sh cmd_add` creates new branches from the canonical repo's current HEAD rather than explicitly basing them on `origin/<default>`. When the canonical's HEAD is anything other than the remote default (stale local `main`/`develop`, long-running feature branch, post-checkout leftover), every new worktree inherits that stale state. Worker PRs then open with a diff surface proportional to the canonical's drift — sometimes hundreds of unrelated files.

## Why

**Canonical failure mode — <webapp>/<webapp>#2716 (scope-leaked PR #2733, 100 files for a 2-line fix):**

1. Dispatched worker created branch `feature/auto-20260424-072814-gh2716` via `worktree-helper.sh add`.
2. `cmd_add` ran `git worktree add -b "$branch" "$path"` without a base ref. Git defaulted to HEAD of the canonical repo.
3. Canonical's HEAD happened to be on stale `main` (commit `c9b8e66c`, "merge develop into main" from April 11 — behind `origin/develop` by many commits).
4. PR opened against `develop` (repo default). Diff = everything `develop` had that `main` didn't + the 2-line fix = 100 files.
5. PR was closed as `CONFLICTING`. Successive cherry-pick retry workers (sonnet → opus-4.6 → opus-4.7) ran out of tokens trying to cherry-pick the 100-file monster into a clean branch. All died at `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` / `no_work` before engaging with the actual 2-line fix.
6. Eventually NMR'd after 2 stale-recovery ticks. Required interactive maintainer intervention to resolve.

**Total cost**: 5+ worker dispatches, opus tokens, maintainer context-switch — to fix a 2-line review comment.

The reuse path in `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:293-305` *does* reset existing worktrees to `origin/<default>` explicitly. The **create** path at `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh:317-320` → `worktree-helper.sh:938` has no equivalent safeguard.

## How

### 1. `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`

Extend `_parse_cmd_add_args` to accept `--base <ref>`:

- New global `_ADD_BASE`.
- New case branches for `--base` and `--base=*`.
- Usage string updated.

In `cmd_add` (new-branch path, around line 938), resolve base ref with precedence:

1. `--base <ref>` if provided (explicit user intent — stacked PR, test fixture, etc.)
2. `origin/$(get_default_branch)` if that ref resolves (`git rev-parse --verify`)
3. `<default_branch>` (local) if remote-tracking doesn't exist
4. Fall back to HEAD (current behaviour) with a `print_warning` if none of the above resolve — surface the degradation so users notice.

Pass the resolved base as the 3rd positional to `git worktree add -b "$branch" "$path" "$base"`.

Log the base used (stderr, `print_info`) so pulse/worker dispatch traces show which base was chosen — critical for future scope-leak debugging.

### 2. `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh`

No code change required — the helper change propagates automatically. Verify by reading the call at line 320 and confirming it doesn't need `--base`.

### 3. Tests

Add a shellcheck verification pass (already covered by CI). For integration, a manual verification matrix:

- Canonical on default branch → worktree branch parent = `origin/<default>` tip. ✔
- Canonical on feature branch → worktree branch parent = `origin/<default>` tip (not feature branch). ✔
- `--base some/other-branch` passed → worktree branch parent = `some/other-branch` tip. ✔
- No `origin` remote (local-only repo) → falls back to local default, logs warning. ✔
- No default branch detectable → falls back to HEAD + loud warning. ✔

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/worktree-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` (only if a log line is added for clarity)

## Acceptance

1. `worktree-helper.sh add <branch>` without `--base` creates the new branch on top of `origin/<default>`, regardless of canonical HEAD.
2. `worktree-helper.sh add <branch> --base <ref>` respects the explicit base.
3. When `origin/<default>` can't be resolved, falls back gracefully and warns.
4. Existing `pulse-dispatch-worker-launch.sh` behaviour preserved — pre-created worktrees are rooted at `origin/<default>` tip.
5. `shellcheck` clean.
6. No regressions in existing worktree usage (local dev, full-loop, stacked PRs).

title: t2804: pulse: diagnose launch_recovery:no_worker_process dispatch stalls (#20702 evidence)
body:
## What

Investigate and remediate the `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` dispatch failure mode. Observed: 7 consecutive pulse worker dispatch attempts on issue #20702 (t2788) failed before a worker process ever spawned. Cascade escalation from `tier:standard` → `tier:thinking` (opus) kept happening but the underlying worker never executed code. Separate from coding-failure loops; this is an orchestration-layer defect.

## Why

Observable evidence (from #20702 issue timeline, 2026-04-24):
- Multiple dispatch claims stamped by runner `alex-solovyev` within minutes
- Each attempt ends with `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` — launch-recovery subsystem observed no live worker
- Cascade tier escalation fired (standard → thinking) as if the worker had failed, but there was no worker to fail
- Interactive takeover via `interactive-session-helper.sh claim` unblocked the issue instantly; human-authored PR landed in ~15 min

This symptom is invisible to the cost-circuit-breaker (no tokens spent since no worker ran) but wastes dispatch slots and triggers NMR escalation incorrectly. If this pattern affects more than one issue or one runner, it's a dispatch-pool availability bug hiding behind "worker failed" classification.

## Decomposition (parent-task)

Investigation first, then phase PRs:

- **Phase 1 — Instrumentation & triage** [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]: collect all `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` events from pulse logs across all runners for last 14 days; classify by runner, issue, tier. Build reproducer or confirm transient.
- **Phase 2 — Root cause** [requires-decision]: inspect `pulse-wrapper.sh` dispatch → spawn path. Candidates: (a) worker launch script exits 0 without spawning, (b) spawn races with dedup guard, (c) canary check passes but `exec` into runtime silently fails, (d) cascade escalation fires on missing worker as if coding failure.
- **Phase 3 — Fix + regression tests** [requires-decision]: address confirmed root cause; add test asserting dispatch = spawn.
- **Phase 4 — Classification improvement** [auto-fire:on-prior-merge]: `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` should NOT trigger cascade tier escalation. It's infra failure, not coding failure. Cascade should retry same tier (or bail) when no worker ever ran.

## How (Phase 1 investigation starting points)

### Files to read

- READ: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — dispatch loop, cascade escalation, launch-recovery entry points
- READ: `.agents/scripts/shared-dispatch-dedup.sh` — dispatch claim/spawn ordering
- READ: `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log` — search for `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` events
- READ: `.agents/scripts/headless-runtime-helper.sh` — how workers actually spawn

### Reference pattern

Model investigation output on `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — already walks the lifecycle (version guard → canary → dispatch → DB isolation → watchdog → recovery) and is natural home for new findings.

### Verification

- Reproducer: integration test mocks failed `exec` to runtime and asserts pulse classifies correctly (not as worker failure)
- Regression: after fix, t2788 class of events produces distinct failure signature (e.g., `launch_recovery:spawn_exec_failed` vs `launch_recovery:no_worker_process`)

## Acceptance (parent-task)

- [ ] Phase 1 PR: instrumentation data collected + classification summary filed
- [ ] Phase 2 PR: root cause identified + documented
- [ ] Phase 3 PR: fix landed + regression test
- [ ] Phase 4 PR: cascade tier escalation no longer triggers on infra failures
- [ ] `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` updated with new failure mode + diagnosis

## Children

- #20763 — t2812: Phase 1 — collect and classify `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` events from pulse logs (`auto-dispatch`, `tier:standard`)
- #20764 — t2813: Phase 2 — identify root cause of `no_worker_process` dispatch failures (`tier:thinking`, blocked by t2812)
- #20765 — t2814: Phase 3 — fix root cause and add regression tests (`tier:thinking`, blocked by t2813)
- #20766 — t2815: Phase 4 — prevent cascade tier escalation on infra failures (`auto-dispatch`, `tier:standard`, blocked by t2814)

## Session Origin

Filed by marcusquinn interactive session while landing t2788 / PR #20736. Multiple dispatch failures on #20702 led to interactive takeover; retrospective shows this is a distinct class from "worker failed while coding".

title: pulse-nmr-approval: scanner-label creation-default check defeats circuit-breaker gate → ever-NMR trap
body:
## Summary

`_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh` runs the **creation-default signature** check before the **circuit-breaker trip** check. The creation-default branch matches on any issue that carries a scanner-provenance label (`source:review-feedback`, `source:review-scanner`, `review-followup`) **regardless of when NMR was applied** — those labels persist for the life of the issue. This short-circuits the circuit-breaker check for every scanner-generated issue that subsequently trips a breaker (stale-recovery, cost, no_work_loop). Auto-approval strips NMR, the `ever-NMR` history flag remains set, and the issue is trapped: `auto-dispatch` label ON, NMR removed, dispatch permanently blocked by `ever-NMR` until a human runs `sudo aidevops approve issue <N>`.

This is the **incomplete half of the t2386 fix** (#19756 post-mortem). t2386 removed breaker markers from the **comment-marker** branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature`, but left the **label-based** branch which is always co-temporal because labels never expire.

## Canonical Evidence

`<webapp>/<webapp>#2717` — a `source:review-feedback` quality-debt issue.

| Time (UTC) | Event | Comment/Log |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-04-24 04:06:53 | Issue created by `quality-feedback-helper.sh scan-merged`, labelled `source:review-feedback`, `tier:standard`, `auto-dispatch` | — |
| 04:26:08 | Worker #1 (alex-solovyev runner) crashed before engaging — `no_work` | stale recovery tick 1/2 |
| 04:41:10 | CLAIM_RELEASED reason=worker_failed | — |
| 04:55:46 | Worker #2 crashed same way | stale recovery tick 2/2 |
| 05:07:24 | **Label `needs-maintainer-review` applied by `stale-recovery-tick:escalated` path** | (label event) |
| 05:07:32 | Comment posted: `<!-- stale-recovery-tick:escalated (threshold=2) -->` | +8s from label event — well inside the ±60s breaker-trip window |
| ~05:07:40 | `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` runs → `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` returns 0 (because `source:review-feedback` label present) → auto-approval **removes NMR** | `[pulse-wrapper] Auto-approved #2717 — maintainer is author, NMR applied by automation` |
| ~05:07:45 | Next dispatch attempt | `[pulse-wrapper] dispatch_with_dedup: BLOCKED #2717 — requires cryptographic approval (ever-NMR)` |
| (ongoing) | Pulse posts `ever-nmr-remediation` comment once; user must manually run `sudo aidevops approve issue 2717` | — |

The circuit-breaker comment at 05:07:32 falls perfectly inside the `label_at ± 60s` window checked by `_nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip`. **That check is never reached** because the label-based branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` returns 0 first.

## Root-cause code reference

`.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`

- **The bug site:** `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (lines 416-456) checks automation-signature **before** circuit-breaker-trip:

    ```bash
    if _nmr_application_has_automation_signature "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
        return 1   # auto-approve OK
    fi
    if _nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
        return 0   # PRESERVE NMR
    fi
    ```

- **The root cause:** the label-based branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (lines 321-329) does not check timing:

    ```bash
    has_bot_label=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/issues/${issue_number}" \
        --jq '[.labels[].name] | map(select(. == "review-followup" or . == "source:review-scanner" or . == "source:review-feedback")) | length' ...)
    if [[ "$has_bot_label" -gt 0 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    ```

    These labels persist for the life of the issue. So any NMR application on a scanner-labelled issue is misclassified as a "creation default" regardless of whether the label event was actually co-temporal with issue creation.

- **The t2386 comment block (lines 253-262) explicitly warns about this failure mode** but only for the marker-based branch. The label-based branch added later (labelled t2686 in the code) re-opened the same hole for a different class of co-temporality violations.

## Fix (recommended)

Invert the check order AND tighten the label-branch to be co-temporal. Defense in depth.

**1. Invert in `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (lines 444-453):**

    if [[ -n "$nmr_at" ]]; then
        # Circuit-breaker check FIRST — the co-temporal marker is a stronger
        # signal than label persistence. Scanner-labelled issues that trip a
        # breaker MUST preserve NMR regardless of creation provenance.
        if _nmr_application_is_circuit_breaker_trip "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
            echo "[pulse-wrapper] ... — circuit breaker tripped — PRESERVING NMR ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
            return 0
        fi
        if _nmr_application_has_automation_signature "$issue_num" "$slug" "$nmr_at"; then
            echo "[pulse-wrapper] ... — creation-default signature detected ..." >>"$LOGFILE"
            return 1
        fi
    fi

**2. Tighten the label-branch in `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (lines 321-329):** only match the scanner label when NMR was applied within N seconds of issue creation — e.g. 5 minutes. Any later NMR event on the same issue is either manual or a breaker trip, not a creation default.

    # Scanner label alone is not sufficient — require the NMR event to have
    # been co-temporal with issue creation (within 300s). Later NMR events
    # on scanner-labelled issues are manual holds or breaker trips.
    local issue_created_at
    issue_created_at=$(gh api "repos/${slug}/issues/${issue_number}" --jq '.created_at' 2>/dev/null)
    if [[ -n "$issue_created_at" && -n "$label_at" ]]; then
        local gap
        gap=$(python3 -c "from datetime import datetime; \
            c=datetime.fromisoformat('$issue_created_at'.replace('Z','+00:00')); \
            l=datetime.fromisoformat('$label_at'.replace('Z','+00:00')); \
            print(int((l-c).total_seconds()))" 2>/dev/null) || gap=999999
        if (( gap <= 300 )); then
            if [[ "$has_bot_label" -gt 0 ]]; then
                return 0
            fi
        fi
    fi

(Approximation — the helper may already have a more idiomatic time-diff utility; prefer that.)

Either fix alone closes this specific case. Both together makes the intent explicit and resilient to future ordering changes.

## Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:444-453` — invert check order in `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer`
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh:321-329` — add creation-time co-temporality guard to label-based branch of `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature`
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh` — regression test

## Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh` — already covers the marker-based classification matrix. The new regression test should extend this pattern with scenarios where a scanner-labelled issue subsequently trips a circuit breaker.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A mock issue with `source:review-feedback` label + NMR applied +60s after a `stale-recovery-tick:escalated` comment → `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` returns 0 (PRESERVE NMR).
2. A mock issue with `source:review-feedback` label + NMR applied at creation time (no breaker comment in window) → still returns 1 (auto-approve OK) — no regression on the happy path.
3. A mock issue with `source:review-feedback` label + NMR applied with neither a creation-time signature nor a breaker marker (pure manual hold at ± 1h from creation) → returns 0 (PRESERVE — manual hold).
4. Existing `test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh` continues to pass unchanged.
5. No-work-loop breaker (`cost-circuit-breaker:no_work_loop`) on a scanner-labelled issue preserves NMR.

## Verification

    bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh
    bash ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh   # new
    shellcheck ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh

## Blast-radius check

One-shot sweep for other trapped issues across all pulse-enabled repos:

    for slug in $(jq -r '.initialized_repos[] | select(.pulse==true and (.local_only//false)==false) | .slug' ~/.config/aidevops/repos.json); do
      gh issue list --repo "$slug" --state open --label "auto-dispatch" --json number,title,labels \
        | jq -r --arg slug "$slug" '.[] | select(.labels | map(.name) | contains(["source:review-feedback"]) or contains(["source:review-scanner"]) or contains(["review-followup"])) | "\($slug)#\(.number) \(.title)"'
    done

For each match, check `aidevops approve verify <N>` — if unverified AND pulse logs show `BLOCKED ... ever-NMR`, it's a survivor of the same trap and needs manual approval.

## Why this wastes user tokens

Every `ever-NMR`-trapped issue requires the maintainer to: (a) notice the ever-nmr-remediation comment, (b) diagnose whether the worker crashes were legitimate infra issues or unimplementable scope, (c) run the crypto-approval command OR pick the issue up interactively (as I'm doing now). Scanner-generated issues are THE most common class of issue in this framework — every quality-debt ticket, every review-followup, every post-merge scanner finding. The trap is likely firing hundreds of times across the network of repos running this framework, each time pulling a human out of flow to crypto-approve a trivial fix whose body already contained the full instructions.

This is also why the symptom is invisible in pulse stats: the wasted tokens aren't worker tokens (workers died pre-engagement), they're **maintainer tokens** — human cognitive load plus the interactive session that unblocks each trapped issue. The framework's token metering doesn't capture this cost.

## Companion investigation

The upstream `no_work` worker crashes that triggered the stale-recovery escalation in the first place need their own investigation (see also #20702 / t2804). That's a separate issue — filing alongside, not blocking this one.

## Session origin

Interactive session against `<webapp>/<webapp>#2717` on 2026-04-24. PR #2781 (idempotent DO-block wrap) ships the user-visible fix; this issue ships the framework-level fix so future occurrences of the same pattern self-recover without manual crypto-approval.

## How

1. Read `_nmr_applied_by_maintainer` (lines 416-456) and `_nmr_application_has_automation_signature` (lines 284-332) — confirm the call graph and the comment intent.
2. Review the t2386 post-mortem commentary at lines 253-267 — the marker-only fix is explained there; this is the companion label-path hole.
3. Apply both fixes (order inversion + label co-temporality).
4. Write the regression test covering the 5 acceptance scenarios.
5. Run existing NMR test suite for regression.
6. Sweep for trapped issues per the Blast-radius section above; post a remediation comment linking this PR on any survivors.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-nmr-approval.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-scanner-label-breaker-trip.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-nmr-automation-signature.sh`

title: issue-sync mislabels open sibling task as status:done when same PR completes a different task
body:
## Symptom

When a PR completes one TODO.md task (e.g. t306 marked `[x]`) and references a different sibling task in the body (e.g. `Ref #1893` for t291, which remains `[ ]`), the post-merge issue-sync run applies `status:done` to the **referenced** issue, not just the resolved one.

Concrete failure: robstiles/qs-agency PR #1941 (merge commit `cf3e03d`).

- PR body: `Resolves #1929` (t306, marked `[x]` on merge) + `Ref #1893` (t291, still `[ ]` in TODO.md)
- Expected post-merge labels on #1893: unchanged (still `status:available`)
- Actual post-merge labels on #1893: `status:done` added by `github-actions[bot]` at 2026-04-24T23:21:21Z, ~16s after merge
- Concurrent (correct) action on same issue at 23:21:31Z: `auto-dispatch` label added (matching new TODO.md tag)

The TODO.md line for t291 was `[ ]` both before and after the merge — there is no signal in the working tree that justifies `status:done`.

## Reproduction

1. Have two open TODO.md entries: A (`[x]`-on-merge) and B (`[ ]`, still pending).
2. Open a PR that closes A via `Resolves #<A-issue>` and merely references B via `Ref #<B-issue>` or `For #<B-issue>`.
3. Merge the PR. Wait for `issue-sync` to run.
4. Observe: B's issue gets `status:done` applied even though B's TODO.md line is still `[ ]`.

## Why this is P2

Wrong `status:done` poisons several pulse paths:

- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` may treat the issue as complete and skip dispatch.
- Cross-repo health dashboards count `status:done` issues as resolved — understates outstanding work.
- Manual triage trusts `status:done` and may close the issue prematurely.

In the concrete case, t291 (#1893) is a real pending production-touching task held behind `needs-maintainer-review`. The incorrect `status:done` would have caused the pulse to skip it entirely once the maintainer cleared NMR.

## Files to inspect

- `.agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh` — TODO ↔ GitHub label sync logic
- `.github/workflows/issue-sync.yml` (or its reusable workflow per t2770) — what triggers and what arguments are passed on `pull_request: closed` events
- Look for any path that iterates `closingIssuesReferences` AND any other body refs (`#NNN` mentions) without distinguishing closing keywords (`Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`) from non-closing keywords (`Ref`/`For`).

The likely culprit: a code path that resolves "all issues referenced in the PR body" and applies `status:done` to all of them, rather than only the issues whose TODO.md line was flipped to `[x]` in the merged commit.

## Expected behaviour

`status:done` should be applied only when:

1. The TODO.md line for that task ID flips from `[ ]` to `[x]` in the merged commit, OR
2. The PR body uses a closing keyword (`Resolves`/`Closes`/`Fixes`) for the issue.

Mere `Ref #N` / `For #N` references must NOT trigger label changes on N.

## Workaround

Manual fix after merge: `gh issue edit <N> --remove-label status:done --add-label status:available`.

## Reference pattern

`scripts/pulse-merge.sh::_extract_linked_issue` already implements the correct closing-keyword-only extraction (per the build.txt rule on `Resolves` vs `Ref`/`For`). Whatever path in `issue-sync-helper.sh` is making this mistake should adopt the same regex semantics: `grep -ioE '(close[ds]?|fix(es|ed)?|resolve[ds]?)\s+#[0-9]+'`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/issue-sync-helper.sh`
- Reproduce on a test repo: open PR with `Resolves #A` + `Ref #B`, merge, confirm B's labels unchanged
- Existing test pattern at `.github/workflows/parent-task-keyword-check.yml` covers the closing-keyword-vs-reference distinction for parent tasks; mirror that test surface for issue-sync.

title: t2816: /setup-git slash command — guided per-repo platform secret setup with toast surfacing (Phase 1)
body:
# t2816 — `/setup-git` slash command: guided per-repo platform secret setup

## Session Origin

Surfaced from interactive triage of `<webapp>/<webapp>#2684` (2026-04-25). The PR #2750 was stuck for ~5h because:

1. Worker created a correct fix → PR opened
2. PR sat with E2E base-drift failures while the planner-fix on `develop` lagged behind
3. t2449 worker-briefed auto-merge gate refused to merge because the linked issue was authored by `github-actions[bot]` (`author_association: NONE`)
4. Bot authorship was caused by **`SYNC_PAT` not being set on `<webapp>/<webapp>`** — the issue-sync workflow falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN` and creates issues as the bot
5. `aidevops security check <webapp>/<webapp>` reports "no branch protection — SYNC_PAT not needed" (FALSE — repo uses **rulesets**, missed by the legacy `/protection` API)

The detector gap is fixed by t2806 (#20745). The discoverability gap remains — even with the advisory firing, the operator gets a one-line `[ADVISORY]` toast and is expected to know to set `SYNC_PAT`. There's no guided path from "I see the advisory" to "the secret is set and verified".

User feedback (verbatim):

> we use the opencode toast to advise how many repos need SYNC_PAT setup, and create/give a command /setup-git or something like that, that will give the instructions for the git platform setup, asking for a list of repo slugs from ~/Git to add to repos.json, what git platform(s) to setup and push those to, and giving links to each repo platform url to add the SYNC_PAT token, remind them to save a copy of the tokens to their password manager, and any other ideas to make sure this setup gets done.

## What

Ship Phase 1 of a guided per-repo platform secret setup flow:

1. **`/setup-git` slash command** (`scripts/commands/setup-git.md`) that walks the operator through fixing per-repo platform secret debt. The command reads existing advisories from `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory`, surfaces the count and slugs, generates platform-specific PAT-creation URLs with required scopes pre-encoded, and walks the operator through `gh secret set` in a separate terminal (NEVER accepts secret values in conversation).

2. **Toast aggregation** — `aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive` emits ONE `[WARN]` summary line aggregating SYNC_PAT-missing repo count when ≥1 advisory exists. The OpenCode plugin's `classifyLines` (`greeting.mjs:172-185`) already buckets `[WARN]` as warning-tier (15s display) — the existing per-repo `[ADVISORY]` lines fall back to info-tier as before. Result: the toast escalates to warning whenever there's setup debt, with a clear `/setup-git` call to action.

3. **`setup-debt-helper.sh`** — small aggregator that reads `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` files, returns the count, slugs, and JSON for both human consumption (slash command) and machine consumption (toast emit, future tests). Subcommands: `summary`, `list-sync-pat-missing`, `verify-secret`, `help`.

4. **Platform matrix reference** (`reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`) — canonical doc with PAT-creation URL templates, scope vocabularies, and `gh`/`glab`/`tea` secret-set commands per platform. GitHub primary; GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket as stubs that point at platform docs (Phase 2 fills these in).

5. **Cross-references** — update `aidevops/onboarding.md` to clarify scope split (`/onboarding` = per-account auth setup; `/setup-git` = per-repo platform secrets), and update `.agents/AGENTS.md` to register `/setup-git` under "Repo registration" and Quick Reference.

6. **Advisory body update** — existing SYNC_PAT advisory body in `security-posture-helper.sh::_emit_sync_pat_advisory` gains one line: "For a guided fix, run `/setup-git` in OpenCode or Claude Code."

## Why

**Discoverability gap.** Today the only path from "I see a SYNC_PAT advisory" to "the PAT is set" is reading the advisory body, then the AGENTS.md "Known limitation — issue-sync TODO auto-completion" section, then the GitHub fine-grained PAT docs, then constructing the right URL with the right scopes by hand. Each step is documented but discoverable only if the operator knows to look. The recurring failure mode (missing SYNC_PAT, bot-authored issues, t2449 blocks auto-merge, PRs sit BLOCKED) is preventable but invisible until something stalls.

**Operational cost.** PR #2750 stalled ~5h before manual takeover. Multiplied across N repos × T months, the unset-PAT class of incident is the dominant cost-of-not-having-a-guided-flow.

**Scaling argument.** Today: 3 repos confirmed at SYNC_PAT issue (`<webapp>/<webapp>`, `essentials-com/essentials.com` missing; `marcusquinn/aidevops` set). At the rate of new-repo creation, this debt grows monotonically without an onboarding path that makes setup the default.

**Existing surface fits.** The integration points already exist:

- Plugin toast (`greeting.mjs`) already classifies `[WARN]` lines.
- Advisory infra already writes `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` files (t2374).
- `opencode-github-setup-helper.sh` already detects platform (GitHub/GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket) and sets up workflows.
- `aidevops/onboarding.md` already covers per-account auth — `/setup-git` is its per-repo complement.

This task composes existing pieces; it doesn't introduce a new architecture.

## How

### Files to modify (Phase 1)

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/setup-debt-helper.sh` (~150 LOC) — aggregator. Subcommands:
  - `summary [--format=human|toast|json]` — count + slug list
  - `list-sync-pat-missing` — one slug per line (one-line stdout, easy to consume)
  - `verify-secret <slug> <name>` — exit 0 if `gh secret list --repo SLUG | grep NAME` finds it
  - `help`
  - Reads `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` (existing format from `_emit_sync_pat_advisory`); applies dismissed-list filter; resolves slug from filename.

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md` (~150 LOC) — slash command spec. Sections:
  - Quick reference (one-line description + invocation)
  - When to use (after a SYNC_PAT advisory toast, after creating a new repo, when onboarding a new operator)
  - Cross-reference to `/onboarding` (different scope)
  - Step-by-step flow for the agent: load setup-debt summary, walk the operator through each gap, generate platform PAT URL, instruct on `gh secret set`, request `verify <slug>` confirmation, write manifest entry (Phase 2).
  - Per-platform URL templates (cross-ref to `reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`)
  - Security posture: never accept secret values in the conversation; never run `gh secret set NAME --body "$VALUE"`; always direct to a separate terminal.

- **NEW**: `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md` (~100 LOC) — platform matrix:
  - GitHub fine-grained PAT URL with query-string scope encoding
  - GitLab personal-access-tokens URL + scope list
  - Gitea / Bitbucket stubs with platform doc links (Phase 2)
  - SecLevel guidance: per-repo over org-wide, expiry rotation, password manager reminder

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh` (~60 LOC) — tests for `summary`, `list-sync-pat-missing`, `verify-secret`. Mocks `~/.aidevops/advisories/` directory; covers zero-advisory, single-advisory, multi-advisory, dismissed-advisory cases.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh:325-360` (`_check_advisories`) — before the per-advisory loop, prepend ONE aggregated `[WARN]` line if `setup-debt-helper.sh summary --format=toast` returns non-empty. The aggregated line is the warning-tier signal; the per-advisory `[ADVISORY]` lines remain as info-tier follow-up detail.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh:631-656` (`_emit_sync_pat_advisory`) — add one line at the top of the advisory body: "For a guided fix, run `/setup-git` in OpenCode or Claude Code."

- **EDIT**: `.agents/aidevops/onboarding.md` — add a "When to use which command" section near the top distinguishing `/onboarding` (per-account auth) from `/setup-git` (per-repo platform secrets). Service Catalog table gains a note: "Per-repo SYNC_PAT setup → `/setup-git`."

- **EDIT**: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — under "Repo registration" subsection, add: "Per-repo platform secret setup (SYNC_PAT etc.): `/setup-git`." Add `/setup-git` to Quick Reference if line budget permits.

### Reference patterns

- Slash command shape: model on `scripts/commands/onboarding.md` (subagent-style command) and `scripts/commands/define.md` (interactive flow command). The new `setup-git.md` is closer to `define.md` — interactive, branching by current state, ends with "verify".
- Helper script shape: model on `setup-local-api-keys.sh` (the "guide and instruct, never accept the secret" precedent) and `opencode-github-setup-helper.sh` (the per-platform detection precedent).
- Toast classification: rely on the EXISTING plugin classifier. No plugin change needed for Phase 1 — adding a `[WARN]`-prefixed line to update-check output is sufficient.
- Advisory aggregation: read `~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-*.advisory` filenames (slug encoded as `OWNER-REPO`); cross-check `dismissed.txt` (existing format). Same pattern as `aidevops-update-check.sh:336-356`.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/setup-debt-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md`
- `.agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh`
- `.agents/aidevops/onboarding.md`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md`

### Verification

```bash
# Local lint
shellcheck .agents/scripts/setup-debt-helper.sh .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh .agents/scripts/security-posture-helper.sh .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh
npx --yes markdownlint-cli2 .agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md .agents/reference/sync-pat-platforms.md .agents/aidevops/onboarding.md .agents/AGENTS.md

# Helper unit tests
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-setup-debt-helper.sh

# Integration with toast
# 1. Create a fake advisory
mkdir -p ~/.aidevops/advisories
cat > ~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-fake-test.advisory <<EOF
[ADVISORY] SYNC_PAT not set for fake/test
EOF
# 2. Run update-check, confirm aggregated [WARN] line appears
bash .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive | grep '\[WARN\] .* repos need SYNC_PAT'
# 3. Cleanup
rm ~/.aidevops/advisories/sync-pat-fake-test.advisory

# Slash command resolution
ls ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/commands/setup-git.md  # post-deploy

# Cross-reference resolution
grep -l "setup-git" .agents/aidevops/onboarding.md .agents/AGENTS.md
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `setup-debt-helper.sh summary --format=toast` returns one `[WARN]`-prefixed line when ≥1 SYNC_PAT advisory exists, empty when none.
- [ ] `aidevops-update-check.sh --interactive` includes the aggregated `[WARN]` line ahead of per-advisory `[ADVISORY]` lines when applicable.
- [ ] `scripts/commands/setup-git.md` exists, follows the slash-command-doc shape, and contains: invocation pattern, when-to-use, cross-reference to `/onboarding`, per-platform PAT URL templates, security-posture warning about secret handling, verify-step.
- [ ] `reference/sync-pat-platforms.md` exists with GitHub URL+scopes (primary) and GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket stubs.
- [ ] `_emit_sync_pat_advisory` advisory body includes the `/setup-git` hint.
- [ ] `aidevops/onboarding.md` and `AGENTS.md` cross-reference `/setup-git` and clarify scope split.
- [ ] `shellcheck` clean on all touched/created shell files.
- [ ] `markdownlint-cli2` clean on all touched/created markdown files.
- [ ] `test-setup-debt-helper.sh` passes (4 cases: zero, single, multi, dismissed).
- [ ] Manual integration test: create fake advisory → update-check shows `[WARN]` → remove fake → update-check no longer shows it.

## Tier

`tier:thinking` — multi-file design surface (helper + slash command + reference doc + plugin/advisory integration), requires evaluating cross-cutting integration points (toast classifier, advisory aggregation, cross-doc references). Phase 1 only — Phases 2 (repo registration auto-fix, multi-platform expansion) and Phase 3 (adjacency: gh auth scopes, AI keys, default branch) are filed as follow-up issues from the merged Phase 1 PR.

## Out of scope (deferred to follow-ups)

- Repo discovery and auto-registration (`/setup-git` Step 1 in design) — Phase 2.

title: t2820: pulse: extend no_work reclassification to worker_failed using Phase 3 log-tail data
body:
## What

Extend the `no_work` classification — which currently triggers only on `launch_recovery:no_worker_process` — to also cover `worker_failed` events where the worker log shows no actual implementation progress (no tool calls, no file edits, no commits). Use the log tail that Phase 3 (t2814, #20765) surfaces to make the decision.

## Why

The current fast-fail classification has two buckets:

1. `no_worker_process` — worker never spawned. t2387 skips tier escalation. Phase 4 (#20766, t2815) will harden the cascade-skip enforcement.
2. `worker_failed` — everything else. Triggers cascade escalation.

But `worker_failed` is a false-merge: it conflates two distinct failure modes that demand opposite responses:

- **Real coding failure**: worker spawned, loaded context (~20K tokens), executed tool calls, produced bad code. Escalation to opus-4-7 is the correct response.
- **Late infra failure**: worker spawned, ran canary, canary passed, then hit a mid-session blip (auth refresh timeout, provider rate limit, plugin hook deadlock) BEFORE any code was produced. Escalation wastes opus tokens on a model that cannot help.

Evidence from #20765:

- Attempt 1 (opus-4-6): `worker_failed` at ~60s — too fast to have written real code; likely an early exit masquerading as coding failure
- Attempt 3 (opus-4-7): `worker_failed` at ~18min — ran but stalled; log tail would reveal whether it produced any file edits

Phase 3 (t2814) lands the log-tail collection in the `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment (`_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` in `pulse-cleanup.sh`). That same log-tail data can drive an automatic reclassification: if the tail shows no tool-call frames after N seconds of runtime, reclassify as `no_work` and trigger the existing t2387 skip-escalation path.

## How

### Prerequisites (blocked-by)

- **Phase 3 (#20765 / t2814)** must merge — delivers the worker-log tail visibility that Fix 1 (`_post_launch_recovery_claim_released`) provides.
- **Phase 4 (#20766 / t2815)** must merge — delivers the distinct `launch_recovery:*` failure signatures and the cascade-skip enforcement that this fix extends.

Do NOT dispatch a worker on this issue until both prerequisites merge. The `no-auto-dispatch` label enforces this.

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — extend `escalate_issue_tier()` (current line ~951) with a reclassification helper that inspects the worker log tail before deciding escalation vs skip.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — extend `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` (current line ~816) to emit the distinct reason it was reclassified (e.g. `no_tool_calls_in_log`, `canary_failure_post_spawn`).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` — extract the log-tail reader from Phase 3's `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` into a shared helper (`_read_worker_log_tail_classified` or similar) so reclassification and claim-released comment share the same parsing logic (DRY).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh` — regression test with fixture log tails for each shape (real-coding-failure, early-exit, mid-session-hang, canary-post-spawn).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document the reclassification signatures.

### Reclassification rules

When fast-fail reason is `worker_failed` AND runtime is under `NO_WORK_RECLASS_ELAPSED_MAX` (default 180s, env-overridable) AND log tail contains **no** `"tool_use"` or `"edit"` step-frames → reclassify as `no_work` with subtype `no_tool_calls_in_log`.

When log tail contains only canary-test output or `[t2814:early_exit]` markers (from Phase 3 Fix 2) → reclassify as `no_work` with subtype `canary_post_spawn_failure`.

When either subtype fires, call the existing `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` path (t2387) with the subtype passed through so the emitted comment explains why escalation was skipped (and which reclassification rule fired).

### Reference pattern

- Model on `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` (worker-lifecycle-common.sh:816) — same output shape, same circuit-breaker integration, same `source:auto-reclassify` provenance marker.
- Log parsing: reuse the log-tail reader from Phase 3 Fix 1 by extracting into `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`. Parsing logic to locate: the body of `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` in `pulse-cleanup.sh` after Phase 3 lands (file path: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`, function added by PR that closes #20765).

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh
# After deploy: observe that worker_failed events under 3 minutes with clean log tails no longer escalate to opus-4-7
# Audit query:
gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/<N>/comments --jq \
  '.[] | select(.body | test("no_work.*(no_tool_calls_in_log|canary_post_spawn_failure)")) | .body' | head -20
```

title: t2821: policy: dispatch-path tasks default to #parent + no-auto-dispatch for interactive implementation
body:
## What

Establish a framework-level rule: tasks whose `## Files to modify` section hits the worker dispatch/spawn path default to `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` unless explicitly overridden. Maintainers implement these interactively rather than through auto-dispatched workers.

## Why

Self-hosting tasks (fixing the worker dispatch path from within worker-dispatched sessions) have a tautology failure mode: broken dispatch kills workers fixing dispatch. Observed on #20765 (t2814):

- 3 worker attempts across ~90 minutes before one succeeded
- 2 attempts failed with `worker_failed`, 1 with `no_worker_process` (the exact bug being fixed)
- Estimated ~40-60K opus tokens burned on failed attempts before the successful opus-4-7 run

Issues A (t2819 — self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override) and B (t2820 — no_work reclassification extension) mitigate the cost **per failed attempt**. This rule addresses the decision to **attempt dispatch at all** for this task class.

The pattern is already encoded for the parent meta-task #20740 (t2804), which uses `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive`. Child phases auto-inherit tier but not this combination — #20765 (Phase 3) carried `auto-dispatch` by default, which kicked off the tautology loop.

Maintainers implementing these interactively have several concrete advantages over auto-dispatched workers:

1. Human context available for judgment calls about dispatch-path design trade-offs
2. Bypass the broken dispatch path entirely (interactive sessions don't spawn workers through the pulse)
3. Unlimited context budget (interactive Claude/OpenCode sessions vs ~200K soft-ceiling for workers)
4. Faster iteration on canary/FD/session-lock logic that requires visibility into the running system
5. The visibility fixes from Phase 3 (Fix 1 worker-log tails in `CLAIM_RELEASED` comments) are most valuable to maintainers debugging live, not to a worker being blocked by the bug

## How

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — add a new section describing the dispatch-path default. Place after "Pre-implementation discovery (t2046)" or within "Worker triage responsibility". Document the trigger file set (shared with Issue A) and the override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/templates/brief-template.md` — add a "Dispatch-path classification" row to the Tier Assignment Validation checklist. If the files-scope section hits the self-hosting set, the tier-checklist flags it and prompts for `#parent`.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/task-brief-helper.sh` — when the brief's `Files Scope` or `How` section references a dispatch-path file, auto-recommend `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` in the TODO entry emitted.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/claim-task-id.sh` — when the `--description` or linked brief hits dispatch-path patterns AND the `--labels` argument includes `auto-dispatch`, emit a stderr warning (not a block) so the user knows what they are overriding.
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-path-parent-default.sh` — regression test for brief-helper + claim-task-id behaviour (positive/negative/override cases).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` — document the default and the manual override path.
- EDIT: `.agents/AGENTS.md` — cross-link the new rule in the "Auto-Dispatch and Completion" section.

### Default decision tree (new)

1. Brief's `Files Scope` or `## How` references any file in the self-hosting set (same canonical list as Issue A — keep it in one place, reference it from both) → recommend `#parent`, `no-auto-dispatch`, and `origin:interactive`.

3. The self-hosting pre-dispatch validator from Issue A (t2819) remains active as a safety net when the override is used, so `model:opus-4-7` is still applied before dispatch.

### Reference pattern

- The `parent-task` label + `no-auto-dispatch` label pattern is already in place — used by #20740 (parent t2804), documented in `reference/parent-task-lifecycle.md`. This rule automates application for a specific file-pattern class.
- The `tier-simple-body-shape-helper.sh` server-side auto-downgrade (t2389) is the closest architectural analogue: detects a mis-classification from the brief shape and adjusts labels with a provenance-wrapped audit comment. Model the brief-helper side-effect on this pattern.

Interactive session with maintainer. Companion policy-level fix to (A) self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override (t2819) and (B) no_work reclassification extension (t2820). All three derived from #20765 dispatch-history analysis.

title: t2825: idempotent task-ID prefix in commit-and-pr (PR title double-prefix fix)
body:
## Session Origin

Surfaced while triaging #20732 dispatch friction (5 attempts → merge). PR #20817 (the recovery PR that closed #20732) ended up titled `t2799: t2799: split RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS from NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS in review-bot-gate-helper` — task-ID prefix appears twice. Cosmetic but visible in the merged-PR audit trail.

## What

In `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`, make the auto-derived PR title prefix idempotent: when `--message` already starts with `t[0-9]+:` or `GH#[0-9]+:`, skip the auto-prefix instead of prepending again.

## Why

`full-loop-helper.sh:1078-1080` currently does:

```bash
if [[ -z "$pr_title" ]]; then
    pr_title="$(_derive_pr_title_prefix "$issue_number"): ${commit_message}"
fi
```

When the worker conscientiously prefixes `--message` with the task ID (the natural form the brief asks for, and the form most workers default to), `_derive_pr_title_prefix` resolves the same prefix from TODO.md and prepends it a second time. Result: `tNNN: tNNN: <description>`.

The issue-sync auto-completion regex (`^tNNN`) tolerates the double-prefix and still extracts a task_id correctly, so the merge-time TODO checkbox flip still works. But the PR title is published in this state, surfaces in `git log --oneline`, and ends up in any audit query that surfaces the title.

This is in the t2821 (#20827) "dispatch-path file" set — `full-loop-helper.sh` is the canonical headless commit/PR pipeline. The proposed t2821 policy says these should default to interactive implementation, which is what this issue does.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1078-1080` — guard the auto-prefix with a regex check.
- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-title-prefix-idempotent.sh` — regression test covering all branches.

### Implementation

Replace lines 1078-1080 with:

```bash
if [[ -z "$pr_title" ]]; then
    if [[ "$commit_message" =~ ^(t[0-9]+|GH#[0-9]+): ]]; then
        # Message already carries a task-ID prefix — use as-is.
        pr_title="$commit_message"
    else
        pr_title="$(_derive_pr_title_prefix "$issue_number"): ${commit_message}"
    fi
fi
```

### Reference patterns

- Regex idiom matches the form already used in `_derive_pr_title_prefix` (line 932) for grep-extracting task IDs from TODO.md.
- Test pattern: model on `.agents/scripts/tests/test-claim-task-id.sh` for the `setup_test_env` / `cleanup_test_env` / `print_result` shape.

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-title-prefix-idempotent.sh
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pr-title-prefix-idempotent.sh`

## Acceptance

1. When `commit_message="t2799: split foo"` and `issue_number=20732` (TODO has `t2799 ... ref:GH#20732`), `pr_title="t2799: split foo"` (no double prefix).
2. When `commit_message="GH#20774: remove alias"` and `issue_number=20774`, `pr_title="GH#20774: remove alias"`.
3. When `commit_message="split foo"` (no prefix) and `issue_number=20732`, `pr_title="t2799: split foo"` (existing behaviour preserved).
4. When `--title "explicit override"` is passed, the new code path is bypassed (existing behaviour preserved — the `[[ -z "$pr_title" ]]` outer guard already handles this).
5. Regression test covers all four cases plus the existing GH#-fallback path.
6. ShellCheck clean.

## Reference

- Bug instance: PR #20817 title `t2799: t2799: split RATE_LIMIT_PATTERNS from NON_REVIEW_PATTERNS in review-bot-gate-helper`
- Related: t2720 (existing tNNN-vs-GH# preference work) at full-loop-helper.sh:886-944
