2. `worker_failed` — everything else. Triggers cascade escalation.

But `worker_failed` is a false-merge: it conflates two distinct failure modes that demand opposite responses:

- **Real coding failure**: worker spawned, loaded context (~20K tokens), executed tool calls, produced bad code. Escalation to opus-4-7 is the correct response.
- **Late infra failure**: worker spawned, ran canary, canary passed, then hit a mid-session blip (auth refresh timeout, provider rate limit, plugin hook deadlock) BEFORE any code was produced. Escalation wastes opus tokens on a model that cannot help.

Evidence from #20765:

- Attempt 1 (opus-4-6): `worker_failed` at ~60s — too fast to have written real code; likely an early exit masquerading as coding failure
- Attempt 3 (opus-4-7): `worker_failed` at ~18min — ran but stalled; log tail would reveal whether it produced any file edits

Phase 3 (t2814) lands the log-tail collection in the `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment (`_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` in `pulse-cleanup.sh`). That same log-tail data can drive an automatic reclassification: if the tail shows no tool-call frames after N seconds of runtime, reclassify as `no_work` and trigger the existing t2387 skip-escalation path.

## How

### Prerequisites (blocked-by)

- **Phase 3 (#20765 / t2814)** must merge — delivers the worker-log tail visibility that Fix 1 (`_post_launch_recovery_claim_released`) provides.
- **Phase 4 (#20766 / t2815)** must merge — delivers the distinct `launch_recovery:*` failure signatures and the cascade-skip enforcement that this fix extends.

Do NOT dispatch a worker on this issue until both prerequisites merge. The `no-auto-dispatch` label enforces this.

### Files to modify

- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — extend `escalate_issue_tier()` (current line ~951) with a reclassification helper that inspects the worker log tail before deciding escalation vs skip.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh` — extend `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` (current line ~816) to emit the distinct reason it was reclassified (e.g. `no_tool_calls_in_log`, `canary_failure_post_spawn`).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` — extract the log-tail reader from Phase 3's `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` into a shared helper (`_read_worker_log_tail_classified` or similar) so reclassification and claim-released comment share the same parsing logic (DRY).
- NEW: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh` — regression test with fixture log tails for each shape (real-coding-failure, early-exit, mid-session-hang, canary-post-spawn).
- EDIT: `.agents/reference/worker-diagnostics.md` — document the reclassification signatures.

### Reclassification rules

When fast-fail reason is `worker_failed` AND runtime is under `NO_WORK_RECLASS_ELAPSED_MAX` (default 180s, env-overridable) AND log tail contains **no** `"tool_use"` or `"edit"` step-frames → reclassify as `no_work` with subtype `no_tool_calls_in_log`.

When log tail contains only canary-test output or `[t2814:early_exit]` markers (from Phase 3 Fix 2) → reclassify as `no_work` with subtype `canary_post_spawn_failure`.

When either subtype fires, call the existing `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` path (t2387) with the subtype passed through so the emitted comment explains why escalation was skipped (and which reclassification rule fired).

### Reference pattern

- Model on `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` (worker-lifecycle-common.sh:816) — same output shape, same circuit-breaker integration, same `source:auto-reclassify` provenance marker.
- The existing `no_worker_process` skip-escalation path (t2387) is the confirmed working reference: per @alex-solovyev's automated escalation-skip notification on #20826, the path correctly skips cascade and emits a `<!-- no-work-escalation-skip -->` comment explaining the no_work rationale.
- Log parsing: reuse the log-tail reader from Phase 3 Fix 1 by extracting into `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh`. Parsing logic to locate: the body of `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` in `pulse-cleanup.sh` (file path: `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`, function added by PR that closes #20765).

### Verification

```bash
shellcheck .agents/scripts/worker-lifecycle-common.sh .agents/scripts/shared-claim-lifecycle.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-no-work-reclassification.sh
# After deploy: observe that worker_failed events under 3 minutes with clean log tails no longer escalate to opus-4-7
# Audit query:
gh api repos/marcusquinn/aidevops/issues/<N>/comments --jq \
  '.[] | select(.body | test("no_work.*(no_tool_calls_in_log|canary_post_spawn_failure)")) | .body' | head -20
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Phase 3 (#20765) and Phase 4 (#20766) merged first (prerequisite check — do not implement until both are deployed)
- [ ] `escalate_issue_tier()` inspects log tail when fast-fail reason is `worker_failed` and runtime is under threshold
- [ ] Distinct reclassification subtypes: `no_tool_calls_in_log`, `canary_post_spawn_failure`
- [ ] Shared log-tail reader extracted to `shared-claim-lifecycle.sh` (DRY with Phase 3 Fix 1)
- [ ] Regression test covers all 4 log shapes (real coding failure / early exit / mid-session hang / canary-post-spawn)
- [ ] Env var override `NO_WORK_RECLASS_ELAPSED_MAX` works
- [ ] `reference/worker-diagnostics.md` updated with the reclassification matrix

## Context & Decisions

**Self-hosting tier override (per @alex-solovyev automated detector):** This issue modifies `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh` (in the log-tail reader extraction) and `worker-lifecycle-common.sh`, both on the dispatch path. Pre-dispatch self-hosting detector (`pre-dispatch-validator-helper.sh`, t2819) applied `model:opus-4-7` on #20826 because workers dispatched to fix dispatch-path code run through the code being fixed — starting at opus-4-6 wastes 1-2 cascade attempts before reaching the tier needed. This issue carries `model:opus-4-7` upfront for the same reason.

**no_worker_process skip path confirmed working (per @alex-soloveyev automated escalation-skip notification):** The t2387 `_log_no_work_skip_escalation` path fires correctly for `no_worker_process` reason. The same path must be reused — not re-implemented — for the new `worker_failed` reclassification subtypes, to maintain consistent comment format and circuit-breaker integration.

**Design constraint:** Reclassification must be opt-in via log-tail availability — if Phase 3's log-tail data is absent (e.g., older dispatch records), fall through to the existing `worker_failed` → escalation behaviour unchanged. No regression on pre-Phase 3 records.

## Session Origin

Interactive session with maintainer. Derived from dispatch-history analysis of #20765 during Phase 3 follow-up. Companion to (A) self-hosting pre-dispatch tier override (t2819) and (C) dispatch-path `#parent` default policy (t2821). All three target the tautology-loop failure mode surfaced by t2804 (#20740).

title: t2832: fix(dispatch-dedup): honour no-auto-dispatch label as unconditional block (parity with parent-task)
body:
## What

Add `no-auto-dispatch` to the unconditional dispatch block list in `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`, alongside the existing `parent-task` / `meta` checks. Currently the label is honoured by enrichment, decomposition, and backfill paths, but **not by the dispatch path itself** — workers get dispatched to issues carrying the label.

## Why

Observed live on #20827 (the very issue establishing the dispatch-path policy that uses this label):

- Issue created at 2026-04-25T00:16:34Z with `no-auto-dispatch` + `origin:interactive` + `tier:standard`
- `alex-solovyev`'s runner stripped `origin:interactive`, added `origin:worker` + `status:queued` at 00:46:13Z
- 6 worker dispatches over 2 hours (00:46 → 02:39), all failing (`no_worker_process` × 2, `worker_failed` × 3, escalated to `tier:thinking` then `model:opus-4-7`)
- Issue eventually consolidated into #20852 and closed `not-planned`
- Estimated ~30-50K opus tokens burned across failed attempts

The bug is that `no-auto-dispatch` is treated as a *don't-modify* signal by some pulse paths but not as a *don't-dispatch* signal by the dispatch path. Static evidence:

```bash
git ls-files '.agents/scripts/pulse*.sh' '.agents/scripts/dispatch*.sh' \
  '.agents/scripts/worker-*.sh' | xargs rg -n 'no-auto-dispatch'
# (no output — zero call sites in the dispatch path)
```

By contrast `parent-task` IS in the unconditional block at `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:644`, which is why the consolidated #20852 policy (t2821) currently has to combine `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` to actually block dispatch. The `#parent` half is doing all the real work; `no-auto-dispatch` alone is an audit-trail signal with no enforcement bite.

This makes `no-auto-dispatch` a footgun: maintainers, agents, and helpers (e.g. `interactive-session-helper.sh lockdown`) reasonably believe it blocks dispatch — and the documentation reinforces that reading — but in practice it only blocks enrichment and decomposition.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:609-665` — extend `_is_assigned_check_parent_task` to also match `no-auto-dispatch`. Either:
  1. Rename the function to `_is_assigned_check_unconditional_block` and broaden the jq `select` clause to `(. == "parent-task" or . == "meta" or . == "no-auto-dispatch")`, emitting a distinct signal token `NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED (label=no-auto-dispatch)` for that case, OR
  2. Add a sibling helper `_is_assigned_check_no_auto_dispatch` modelled on the existing one and wire it into the same call site at `:861`.

   Approach (1) is preferred — single jq pass, single audit comment shape, consistent error handling for the `_jq_rc` fail-closed case (t2061).

- **EDIT**: `.agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh:861` (the existing `_is_assigned_check_parent_task` call site) — update the comment to reflect the broader unconditional-block set, no logic change needed if option (1) is taken.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf` — add `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` to the list. Currently the conf references `pulse-dispatch-` (substring match catches `pulse-dispatch-dedup-layers.sh`) but not `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` itself. The pre-dispatch detector (t2819) should flag this file too.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md` — replace any "use `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` because the latter doesn't block on its own" caveats with the post-fix reality. Document `NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED` as a recognised dispatch-dedup signal alongside `PARENT_TASK_BLOCKED`.

- **EDIT**: `.agents/prompts/build.txt` — the "Dispatch-path default (t2821)" section currently mandates `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` + `#interactive`. Once this fix lands, `no-auto-dispatch` + `#interactive` is sufficient for non-decomposable focused fixes; `#parent` should be reserved for actual decomposition trackers. Update the rule to prefer the lighter combination unless the task genuinely needs phase decomposition.

- **NEW**: `.agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-no-auto-dispatch-block.sh` — regression test: build a fake `meta_json` containing `no-auto-dispatch`, call `_is_assigned_check_parent_task` (or its renamed successor), assert exit 0 + `NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED` signal. Negative case: meta_json without the label returns exit 1. jq-failure case still emits `GUARD_UNCERTAIN` (t2061 fail-closed preserved).

### Files Scope

- .agents/scripts/dispatch-dedup-helper.sh
- .agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf
- .agents/reference/auto-dispatch.md
- .agents/prompts/build.txt
- .agents/scripts/tests/test-dispatch-dedup-no-auto-dispatch-block.sh

### Complexity Impact

```bash
# expect: NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED on stdout, exit 0 (block dispatch)

# Live verification: re-test against the historical evidence on #20827 —
# replay the dispatch decision against the post-fix code path with the
# captured meta_json, expect block instead of dispatch.
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` blocks dispatch when `no-auto-dispatch` is on the issue's labels (parity with `parent-task` block)
- [ ] Distinct signal `NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED (label=no-auto-dispatch)` emitted for caller pattern matching
- [ ] Fail-closed jq error handling preserved (t2061 contract intact)
- [ ] `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh` added to `self-hosting-files.conf` so future tasks touching this file are auto-flagged
- [ ] Regression test covers positive / negative / jq-failure cases
- [ ] `reference/auto-dispatch.md` updated to document `NO_AUTO_DISPATCH_BLOCKED` and remove the "no-auto-dispatch is audit-only" caveats
- [ ] `prompts/build.txt` "Dispatch-path default (t2821)" section updated: `no-auto-dispatch` + `#interactive` is sufficient for focused fixes; `#parent` reserved for actual decomposition
- [ ] ShellCheck clean

Filed from interactive session with maintainer (2026-04-25). Triggered by the question "why is #20827 no-auto-dispatch?" — investigation revealed the label was deliberately applied by the maintainer at issue creation, but `alex-solovyev`'s runner dispatched 6 workers anyway because the dispatch path doesn't honour the label.

This is an enforcement gap, not a policy gap. The consolidated #20852 (t2821) addresses the *creation* layer (auto-recommend `#parent` + `no-auto-dispatch` for dispatch-path tasks). This issue addresses the *enforcement* layer (make the label do what it says on the tin).

## Tier

`tier:standard` — Sonnet. Single small extension to an existing helper, mirrors a well-established pattern, requires a regression test and doc updates. Not simple (touches dispatch path, requires care around fail-closed contract, multiple coordinated file edits). Not thinking (no novel design — strict mirror of `parent-task` precedent).

This issue is intentionally filed with `no-auto-dispatch` + `#interactive` (no `#parent` because it does not need decomposition) — dispatch-path changes should be reviewed and implemented by the maintainer interactively per the t2821 policy. Until this fix lands, the `no-auto-dispatch` label on this very issue does not actually block dispatch — that's exactly the bug being fixed. If a worker picks it up via the dedup-bypass it documents, that's evidence of the bug, not a workflow problem.

title: t2840: knowledge / cases / matter framework planes (MVP)
body:
## What

Establishes a standardised framework primitive — `_knowledge/`, `_cases/` and supporting infrastructure — applicable to any aidevops-managed repo. Serves multiple matter types (code projects, business cases, limited companies, asset portfolios, customer relationships, investigations, research projects) via the same engine, parallel to existing `.agents/`, `TODO.md`, `todo/`.

**MVP scope (this parent):** 6 phases, 16 children covering knowledge plane skeleton, sensitivity classification + LLM routing, kind-aware enrichment, cases plane, email channel, and AI comms agent.

**Full design context:** see `todo/tasks/t2840-brief.md` (committed on branch `feature/t2840-knowledge-planes-mvp`, planning PR pending).

## Why

The same ingestion-index-retrieve pattern serves any long-running matter with documents around it. Building one engine means:

- Technical agents get queryable knowledge (vendor docs, recurring decisions, industry patterns)
- Business cases get evidence management + AI-drafted comms (disputes, complaints, breaches, debts)
- Limited companies get statutory document storage with audit trails
- Asset portfolios get maintenance + incident histories
- webapp t357 (file post-processing pipeline) becomes a thin SaaS layer over the same engine

Without this primitive: every repo needing document-shaped data invents its own ingestion + index + retrieval. With it: standardised, audit-trailed, sensitivity-aware, retrievable across all aidevops-managed repos via one CLI surface.

## Phases & Children (20 total)

Phases pre-filed (not auto-fired) for parallelism within phases. Cross-phase dependencies enforce ordering.

### P0 — knowledge plane skeleton (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2844 / #20896 | P0a: knowledge plane directory contract + provisioning |
| t2843 / #20895 | P0b: knowledge CLI surface (add/list/search) + platform abstraction |
| t2845 / #20897 | P0c: knowledge review gate routine + NMR integration |

### P0.5 — sensitivity + LLM routing layer (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2846 / #20899 | P0.5a: sensitivity classification schema + detector |
| t2847 / #20900 | P0.5b: LLM routing helper + audit log |
| t2848 / #20901 | P0.5c: Ollama integration + local LLM substrate |

### P1 — kind-aware enrichment (2 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2849 / #20902 | P1a: kind-aware enrichment + structured field extraction |
| t2850 / #20903 | P1c: PageIndex tree generation across corpus |


### P2 — `_inbox/` capture & triage (4 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2866 / #20930 | P2a: `_inbox/` directory contract + per-repo provisioning |
| t2867 / #20931 | P2b: inbox capture CLI + watch folder + audit log |
| t2868 / #20932 | P2c: inbox triage routine: sensitivity gate → classification → routing |
| t2869 / #20933 | P2d: pulse digest of stale inbox items + weekly review surface |

### P4 — cases plane (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2851 / #20904 | P4a: case dossier contract + `aidevops case open` |
| t2852 / #20905 | P4b: case CLI surface (attach/status/close/archive/list) |
| t2853 / #20906 | P4c: case milestone + deadline alarming routine |

### P5 — email channel (3 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2854 / #20908 | P5a: `.eml` ingestion handler (kind=email) |
| t2855 / #20909 | P5b: IMAP polling routine + `mailboxes.json` registry |
| t2856 / #20910 | P5c: email thread reconstruction + filter→case-attach |

### P6 — AI comms agent (2 children)

| Child | Title |
|---|---|
| t2857 / #20911 | P6a: `aidevops case draft` agent (RAG, human-gated, provenance) — `tier:thinking` |
| t2858 / #20912 | P6b: `aidevops case chase` (template-only, opt-in auto-send) |

## MVP Exit Criteria (when all 20 children merged)

- [ ] `aidevops knowledge add <path>` works for a PDF, a URL, an `.eml`
- [ ] `aidevops inbox add <path>` captures into `_inbox/` with audit-log entry
- [ ] `aidevops inbox triage` routes items to planes with sensitivity-first gating; privileged content never reaches cloud LLM
- [ ] `aidevops case open <slug>` creates a case dossier
- [ ] `aidevops case draft <case>` produces a draft with provenance footer (human-gated)
- [ ] `aidevops case chase <case> --template <name>` sends a template-only chaser (opt-in)
- [ ] Sensitivity classification stamps every source's `meta.json`
- [ ] LLM routing fails hard if no compliant provider for a tier
- [ ] Provisioning works in a `local_only: true` repo (no GitHub)
- [ ] Standard skeleton provisions in any new aidevops-init repo

## Cross-Phase Dependencies

- P0.5 children blocked by P0a (need plane substrate to stamp meta.json)
- P1 children blocked by P0a + P0b (need directory contract + CLI before structured extraction)
- P2a/P2b can ship in parallel with P0 (independent directory contract)
- P2c blocked by P0.5a + P0.5c (sensitivity-first triage requires local detector + Ollama)
- P2d blocked by P2c (digest reads from triage.log)
- P4 children blocked by P0a + P0b + P0.5a (cases plane uses sensitivity stamps)
- P5 children blocked by P0a + P0b + P1a (email is a kind of knowledge ingestion)
- P5c blocked by P4a + P4b (filter→case-attach uses case CLI)
- P6 blocked by P4 + P1c + P0.5b/c (drafts use cases, RAG, LLM routing)

Within each phase, children that don't depend on each other can run in parallel; children depending on others wait.

## Out of MVP Scope (post-MVP follow-on)

Filed under separate parent after MVP exit:

- **`_campaigns/` plane** — marketing/ads/outreach work. Filed as **t2870 / #20929** (peer parent-task, decomposes into 6 future phases).
- **Structured tag format (Markdoc-style)** — crosscutting content format for inline semantic tags (`{% sensitivity %}`, `{% citation %}`, `{% case-attach %}`, `{% provenance %}`) across all planes. Filed as **t2874 / #20966** (peer parent-task, 7 future phases). t2849 + t2850 ship forward-compat hooks (draft tag emission + tag-aware tree metadata) so phase 4-5 of t2874 swap parsers without re-wiring producer/consumer.
- P1b: auto-transcription pipeline (manual `.md` drops work without it)
- Additional ingestion channels: URL fetching, GH-issue ingestion (separate from `_inbox/` triage which IS in MVP)
- `_performance/` plane (KPI tracking, metrics, dashboards)
- `_feedback/` plane (capability-gap mining)
- `_projects/` plane
- `_contacts-index/` and `_accounts-index/` adapters
- Gitea/GitLab adapter implementation (abstraction layer ships in MVP, gh-only impl)
- webapp t357 SaaS layer (thin wrapper over framework engine)

## Reference

- Full design: `todo/tasks/t2840-brief.md`
- Per-child briefs: `todo/tasks/t2843-brief.md` through `todo/tasks/t2858-brief.md` (skipping t2841/t2842 which other sessions claimed); P2 phase children at `todo/tasks/t2866-brief.md` through `todo/tasks/t2869-brief.md`

- Final phase child PR: uses `Closes #20892` to close this parent

title: t2841: pulse-issue-reconcile: _b_nums unbound when issue body has no children-section
body:
## Task

Fix unbound variable error in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh::_extract_child_numbers` (line 2007). The `_b_nums` local is only assigned when the issue body contains a `## Sub-issues` (or similar) section. When the section is absent, the conditional branch at line 1997-2000 is skipped, leaving `_b_nums` unset. Line 2006-2007 then references `$_b_nums` under `set -u`, killing the function.

## Why

Observable failure in the deployed pulse log:

```
/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh: line 2007: _b_nums: unbound variable
/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh: line 2007: _b_nums: unbound variable
/Users/marcusquinn/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh: line 2007: _b_nums: unbound variable
```

(Three back-to-back hits, same instance — every parent-task reconcile pass for an issue without a children-section dies.)

Impact: parent-task reconciliation silently fails for any parent issue whose body lacks a `## Sub-issues` (or equivalent) section. The function returns mid-execution, so:

- Parent-task auto-close (t2442) may not detect that all children are merged
- Parent-task nudge/escalate flow (t2771/t2388) may not fire
- Source-label tracking (`graph+body+prose`) is incomplete

This is a regression — the comment at line 1990 introduced the dash-joined source-label tracking, and the `if [[ -n "$children_section" ]]` guard was added to avoid running the body-extractor on empty input. The local declaration includes `_b_nums` but never initialises it.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:1990` — initialise `_b_nums=""` at declaration

### The fix (one line)

Change line 1990 from:

```bash
local _g_nums _b_nums _p_nums child_nums
```

to:

```bash
local _g_nums="" _b_nums="" _p_nums="" child_nums=""
```

This matches the pattern used elsewhere in the file (e.g., `local _src_parts=""` on line 1991) and ensures all three extractors-output variables have a defined value when the union concat runs at line 2006.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Source the script with set -u and a stubbed call
bash -c 'set -u; source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh; _extract_child_numbers 1 owner/repo "Body without children section"' 2>&1
# Should NOT output "unbound variable" — should return cleanly

# 2. Watch pulse log after deploy — no more _b_nums errors
tail -f ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-wrapper.log | grep _b_nums
```

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_b_nums`, `_g_nums`, `_p_nums`, `child_nums` all initialised to `""` at declaration
- [ ] No `unbound variable` errors in pulse-wrapper.log after deploy
- [ ] shellcheck clean on changed file

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`

## Session Origin

Discovered in interactive session t2835 (PR #20887) while investigating <webapp> PR pile-up. Bug visible in pulse-wrapper.log timestamped 2026-04-25. Three back-to-back errors per cycle suggest every reconcile pass against an issue without a children-section is hitting this.

title: t2842: full-loop-helper commit-and-pr: run project linters/formatters/typecheck before push (close worker-CI-failure gap)
body:
## Task

Add a `_run_project_validators` step to `full-loop-helper.sh::cmd_commit_and_pr` that runs the project's standard format/lint/typecheck commands BEFORE the rebase-and-push, with auto-fix where possible. Eliminates the "worker pushes code that fails CI" failure mode.

## Why

**Observable failure (interactive triage of 16 stuck <webapp> PRs, 2026-04-25):**

12 of 16 stuck PRs have at least one of `Format`, `Lint`, or `Typecheck` failing. Pattern:

| PR | Failures |
|---|---|
| #2948 | Lint, Typecheck |
| #2984 | Lint, Typecheck |
| #2991 | Lint, Typecheck |
| #3014 | Format, Lint, Typecheck |
| #3017 | Typecheck |
| #3022 | Lint |
| #3024 | Format |
| #3025 | Format |
| ... | ... |

**Root cause:** <webapp>'s `.git/hooks/pre-commit` only flushes `bd` (beads) state — it does NOT run prettier/eslint/tsc. Workers commit unvalidated code through `full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr`, push, CI fails 5+ minutes later. The pulse has no auto-redispatch for CI-failure-only PRs (different from conflict-feedback), so these accumulate indefinitely.

**Cost so far:** 8 PRs sitting 0-10h, each consumed 1 worker session worth of tokens to produce, all need fix-up touch from a human or another worker. Net loss of ~8 worker-sessions of work.

**Why this is the right layer:** the framework already runs through `cmd_commit_and_pr` for every worker-produced PR. Adding the validator step here catches the gap once for ALL projects, regardless of whether they have project-specific pre-commit hooks. Project-side hooks remain correct as defense-in-depth, but framework can't assume they exist.

## How

### Files to modify

- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh:1119` (`cmd_commit_and_pr`) — insert `_run_project_validators` call between `_stage_and_commit` (line 660) and `_rebase_and_push` (line 688)
- **EDIT:** `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh` — add new function `_run_project_validators` near `_stage_and_commit`
- **REFERENCE:** `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh` — existing aidevops linter runner; same pattern but project-aware

### Approach

Add `_run_project_validators "$skip_hooks"` step. The function:

1. **Detect project type** by file presence:
   - `package.json` with `scripts.format`/`scripts.lint`/`scripts.typecheck` → npm/pnpm/yarn project
   - `Cargo.toml` → Rust → `cargo fmt && cargo clippy && cargo check`
   - `pyproject.toml` → Python → `ruff format && ruff check && mypy` (if configured)
   - `*.go` files → `gofmt -w . && go vet`
   - None → log `[validators] no project detected, skipping` and return 0
2. **Run available auto-fixers first** (format:fix, lint:fix). Re-stage if files changed.
3. **Run check-only validators** (typecheck). Failures → return 1 with clear error pointing to the failing command and suggesting `--skip-hooks` for known-safe doc-only changes.
4. **Detect package manager** from lockfile presence (`pnpm-lock.yaml` → pnpm; `yarn.lock` → yarn; `package-lock.json` → npm).

Detection heuristic for npm-style script names (try in order, use first that exists in `package.json::scripts`):
- Format: `format:fix`, `format:write`, `prettier:fix`, `format`
- Lint: `lint:fix`, `lint:eslint:fix`, `lint`
- Typecheck: `typecheck`, `tsc`, `check:types`

### Skip / opt-out

- `--skip-hooks` arg (existing) — bypasses entirely
- `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1` env — global bypass for emergency cases
- Auto-skip if commit message starts with `wip:` (intermediate WIP commits don't need full validation)
- Auto-skip if only docs changed (`*.md`, `*.txt`, `LICENSE`) — same logic as Qlty regression gate's docs-only path

### Verification

```bash
# In <webapp> worktree, intentionally introduce a lint error
echo 'const x="bad"' >> apps/web/src/test.ts
full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 1234 --message "test: validator should catch this"
# EXPECTED: commit succeeds (auto-fix applies), or push blocked with clear error if typecheck fails

# Test bypass
full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 1234 --message "test: skip" --skip-hooks
# EXPECTED: no validator step, push proceeds

# Test no-project
cd /tmp/empty && git init && touch foo
full-loop-helper.sh commit-and-pr --issue 1234 --message "test: no project"
# EXPECTED: log "no project detected, skipping" and proceeds
```

### Release path

- Bump version: `version-manager.sh release patch`
- Deploy: `setup.sh --non-interactive` (auto-restarts pulse t2579)
- Monitor: watch <webapp> PRs over 24h — new PRs from workers should NOT have Format/Lint/Typecheck failures

## Acceptance

- [ ] `_run_project_validators` function added, detects npm/pnpm/yarn projects
- [ ] Format and Lint auto-fix step runs and re-stages changes if any
- [ ] Typecheck step runs check-only and blocks push on failure with mentor error
- [ ] `--skip-hooks` and `AIDEVOPS_SKIP_PROJECT_VALIDATORS=1` both bypass
- [ ] WIP commits and docs-only PRs auto-skipped
- [ ] Tested in <webapp> worktree with intentional lint error → caught and fixed
- [ ] No regression on aidevops own commits (the script already runs without project-side npm scripts)
- [ ] Release bumped, deployed, pulse restarted
- [ ] 24h monitoring window: new <webapp> PRs from workers show 0 Format/Lint failures

## Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper.sh`
- `.agents/AGENTS.md` (mention the new step in commit-and-pr docs)
- `.agents/VERSION` (release bump)

body:
P0.5c: Ollama integration + local LLM substrate #framework parent:t2840

## Worker Guidance


1. **Extend `ollama-helper.sh` with three subcommands:**
   - `chat`: validates model exists (auto-pull if missing), reads prompt file, calls `ollama run <model> < prompt-file`, captures output (with timeout), returns completion. Honour `--max-tokens` (passes to model parameters), `--temperature`.
   - `embed`: similar pattern, calls `ollama embed`, returns JSON array of floats.
   - `health`: `ollama list` (succeeds → daemon up), check at least one model installed.
2. **Auto-start logic** — function `_ensure_running()`:
   - `health` check; if down, log "starting ollama"; call existing `serve` subcommand; poll `health` every 1s for 30s; on timeout, exit 2 with explanatory message.
3. **Recommended bundle config** — `~/.aidevops/configs/ollama-bundle.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "fast":      { "model": "llama3.1:8b",  "purpose": "classify, short-form summary" },
     "reasoning": { "model": "llama3.1:70b", "purpose": "drafts, structured extraction, long-form" },
     "embed":     { "model": "nomic-embed-text", "purpose": "vector embeddings" }
   }
   ```
   On first `chat` call, ensure all three pulled (or warn user with disk-space estimate).
4. **Privacy check** — `privacy-check` subcommand:
   - Spawn `ollama run` on a known fixed prompt with a network-monitor wrapper (e.g. `lsof -i` on the ollama process, or a stub that asserts the process has no outbound TCP except to localhost ollama daemon)

# t2853: case milestone + deadline alarming routine

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: `pulse routine cron alarming reminder` → existing pulse routines pattern in `TODO.md` `## Routines`
- [x] Discovery: `pulse-wrapper.sh` is the routine integration point; sibling routines like nightly triage already work
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`, `.agents/reference/routines.md`
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — routine + reminder logic; pulse-driven, no daemon

## Origin

- Created: 2026-04-25
- Parent task: t2840 / GH#20892
- Phase: P4 (cases plane)

## What

A pulse-driven routine that reads all open cases' deadlines, classifies each by urgency (red ≤7d, amber ≤30d, green >30d), and alarms via configurable channel (default: GH issue + ntfy notification + audit log). Sub-minute latency on legal deadlines is theatre — pulse polling (5-15min) is sufficient and avoids a daemon.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh tick` — pulse-driven routine: scan all open cases' deadlines, classify, alarm if not already alarmed at this stage
2. Stage memory: `_cases/.alarm-state.json` records last-alarmed stage per (case-id, deadline-label) so re-runs don't spam
3. Config in `_config/case-alarms.json`: stages (default: `[7, 30]` days), channels (default: `["gh-issue", "ntfy"]`), per-case overrides
4. Alarm channels:
   - `gh-issue` — open a GH issue tagged `kind:case-alarm` with case-id + deadline + days-remaining; auto-close on next tick if deadline now passed or removed
   - `ntfy` — push notification (uses existing `aidevops` ntfy infrastructure if present)
   - `email` — stub for MVP (full email send arrives in P5)
5. Routine `r043` in `TODO.md` `## Routines`, repeat: `cron(*/15 * * * *)`, run: `scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh tick`
6. Manual: `aidevops case alarm-test <case-id>` — re-fires alarms once for a case (testing/debug)

## Why

Cases without deadline visibility get missed. Filing deadlines, statute-of-limitations dates, contractually-required notice periods — missing one of these has tangible cost (a dispute conceded, a contract auto-renewed, a regulatory penalty). The framework's job is to make missing them require active dismissal, not passive forgetfulness.

Pulse-based alarming (rather than a separate daemon) reuses existing infrastructure: the pulse already runs every 5 min, has lifecycle and lock primitives, and can dispatch alerts via existing channels. A separate alarm daemon would be parallel infrastructure for no functional gain.

## How (Approach)

1. **Alarm config** — `.agents/templates/case-alarms-config.json`:
   ```json
   {
     "stages_days": [30, 7, 1],
     "channels":    ["gh-issue", "ntfy"],
     "ntfy_topic":  "aidevops-case-alarms",
     "per_case_overrides": { "case-2026-0001-foo": { "stages_days": [60, 14, 3] } }
   }
   ```
2. **Alarm helper** — `scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh`:
   - `tick`: list all `_cases/case-*` (not archived); for each, read `dossier.toon.deadlines`; for each deadline, compute `days_until = (deadline_date - now)`; classify against stages (`green` if > max stage, `amber/red` between stages); for each `(case-id, deadline-label)` not yet alarmed at current stage, fire alarm; record in `.alarm-state.json`
   - `alarm-test <case-id>`: bypass stage memory, fire alarms for all deadlines once
   - `_alarm_gh-issue <case-id> <deadline> <days>` — opens GH issue, returns issue number; subsequent calls update or close the issue
   - `_alarm_ntfy <case-id> <deadline> <days>` — POST to configured ntfy topic
3. **Stage memory** — `_cases/.alarm-state.json`:
   ```json
   { "case-2026-0001-foo": { "filing-deadline-2026-08-31": "amber" } }
   ```
   On re-tick: only fire if computed-stage > recorded-stage (escalation). Auto-close GH alarm issues when deadline passes (timeline entry; alarm record cleared).
4. **GH issue lifecycle** — alarm issues use a stable title pattern (`Case alarm: <case-id> deadline <label>`) so re-tick updates rather than duplicates; closed when deadline passes or alarm cleared
5. **Routine `r043`** — append to `TODO.md` `## Routines`; pulse picks up automatically; lock-protected (only one alarm tick per cycle)
6. **Tests** — covers stage classification, no-spam (re-tick same stage), escalation (amber→red), gh-issue lifecycle, ntfy stub send, per-case override, archived cases ignored

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/case-alarm-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/templates/case-alarms-config.json`
- EDIT: `.agents/cli/aidevops` (add `case alarm-test` subcommand)
- EDIT: `TODO.md` (add `r043` routine entry — done in this task's PR)
- NEW: `.agents/tests/test-case-alarm.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/cases-plane.md` (alarming section)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `case-alarm-helper.sh tick` finds all open cases with future deadlines and classifies each by stage
- [ ] First tick at `red` stage opens a GH issue tagged `kind:case-alarm`
- [ ] Second tick at same stage does NOT open duplicate issue (stage memory)
- [ ] Escalation tick (amber → red): updates existing alarm issue with new severity comment
- [ ] Deadline passes: alarm issue auto-closes with summary timeline entry
- [ ] `--ntfy` configured: POST sent to topic with case-id + days-remaining + label
- [ ] Per-case override: case with `stages_days: [60, 14, 3]` alarms at 60d not 30d
- [ ] Archived cases are skipped
- [ ] Routine runs every 15 min on the pulse, lock-protected (no overlap)
- [ ] `aidevops case alarm-test <case-id>`: forces re-fire for testing without bumping stage memory
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations
- [ ] Tests pass: `bash .agents/tests/test-case-alarm.sh`

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** t2851 (P4a — cases must exist with deadlines), t2852 (P4b — case list, status filtering)
- **Soft-blocked by:** none for MVP (email channel arrives in P5; for MVP, ntfy + GH-issue are enough)
- **Blocks:** none (final P4 leaf)

   ```json
         "folders": ["INBOX", "Cases/2026"],
         "since": "2026-01-01"
       }
     ]
   }
   ```
2. **Poll helper** — Python script `scripts/email_poll.py` using `imaplib` (stdlib):
   - For each configured mailbox: connect, login, select folder
   - `UID FETCH <last+1>:* (RFC822 UID)` to get new messages since last-seen UID
   - For each fetched message: write `.eml` to `_knowledge/inbox/email-<mailbox-id>-<uid>.eml`
   - Update state with new high-watermark UID

Two related capabilities that together close the email→cases loop:

2. **Filter → case-attach** — sieve-style rules in `_config/email-filters.json` that match incoming emails (post-ingestion) against rules; matching emails get attached to the configured case via `case-helper.sh attach` automatically. Audit-logged.

## Worker Guidance


1. **RAG retrieval** — `case-draft-helper.sh draft`:
   - Read `dossier.toon` for case context (parties, kind, status, recent timeline)
   - Read `sources.toon` for attached source IDs
   - Compose retrieval intent: `"<user-provided intent>; case kind: <kind>; parties: <parties>"` 
   - Call `knowledge-index-helper.sh query --intent "..." --scope case=<case-id>` (extension to t2850's CLI)
   - Retrieve top N=8 excerpts with anchors; cap total context size (8K tokens for short drafts, 32K for long)
2. **Tier resolution** — `_max_tier(sources)`: pick maximum sensitivity over all attached sources for the case. Use this as `--tier` to `llm-routing-helper.sh route`. If `privileged`, also force `--task draft` and let routing layer hard-fail if Ollama down.
3. **Prompt template** — `templates/case-draft-prompt.md`:
   ```
   You are drafting a {tone} {kind} for case {case-id} on behalf of {party-self}.
   The intent is: {intent}.
   Recent case timeline: {last 5 timeline entries}.
   Available evidence:
   {numbered list of excerpts with [source-id]: "excerpt..." anchors}
   
   Produce a draft that:
   - Cites every claim with [source-id] anchors
   - Stays {tone}; avoids speculation beyond the evidence
   - Length: {length}
   At the end, list "Drafted with reference to:" with each consulted source.
   ```
4. **Output writing** — write to `_cases/<case-id>/drafts/<timestamp>-<intent-slug>.md`:
   - Markdown with frontmatter: `case_id, intent, tone, length, model, generated_at, sources_consulted, cross_case_includes`
   - Body: the LLM output verbatim
   - Provenance footer (auto-appended even if model omits it): explicit list of source-ids with kind + sensitivity + sha
5. **Cross-case access** — `--include-case <id>`: validates `<id>` exists, appends audit entry to `_cases/<self-case-id>/comms/cross-case-access.jsonl` `{at, included_case, included_by, reason?}`, then queries that case's sources too
6. **Tone library** — `_config/draft-tones.json` defines tone presets (system-prompt fragments) so users can add custom tones per repo
7. **Revise mode** — `--revise <file> --feedback "..."`:
   - Read existing draft
   - Compose prompt: `"Revise this draft per feedback: {feedback}. Original draft: {body}"`
   - Same routing path; new file at `_cases/<case-id>/drafts/<timestamp>-<intent>-rev2.md`
8. **Tests** — covers happy path with mocked LLM, tier escalation when privileged-attached, cross-case access requires `--include-case` flag, provenance footer always present, revise mode preserves prior context

Drafts are **always human-gated** — the helper writes to `_cases/<case-id>/drafts/<timestamp>-<intent-slug>.md` and never auto-sends.

**Concrete deliverables:**

1. `scripts/case-draft-helper.sh draft <case-id> --intent "..." [flags]` — generates draft, writes to drafts/, opens preview
2. Default scope: only `_knowledge/sources/<id>/` for sources in this case's `sources.toon`. Cross-case access via `--include-case <id>` (logged in `_cases/<case-id>/comms/cross-case-access.jsonl` for audit)
3. RAG composition: tree-walk via `knowledge-index-helper.sh query` (case-scoped) → top N excerpts → LLM call via `llm-routing-helper.sh route --tier <max-of-source-tiers>` with prompt that mandates evidence citation
4. Provenance footer (mandatory in every draft): "Drafted with reference to: source-id (kind: invoice, sensitivity: pii, sha: abc...), source-id, ... Generated by: aidevops v.X.Y, model: <name>, at: <timestamp>"
5. Tier escalation: if any source attached to the case is `privileged`, the draft routes through local LLM (Ollama via t2848) — no cloud calls, hard fail if Ollama down
6. CLI flags: `--intent <free-text>`, `--tone <neutral|formal|conciliatory|firm>`, `--length <short|medium|long>`, `--cite <strict|loose>`, `--dry-run` (print draft to stdout, don't write)
7. Re-draft: `aidevops case draft <case-id> --revise <draft-file> --feedback "..."` reads existing draft + feedback, generates revision

## Why

Strategic communications carry weight — a misworded dispute response or contract clause can have material consequences. AI drafting reduces blank-page friction (10x productivity gain on first-draft work) but final approval must be human. Auto-send for strategic comms is forbidden (P6b handles routine chasers).

Provenance footers serve two purposes: (1) the human can verify the draft cites the right sources before sending, (2) the audit trail shows exactly which knowledge was consulted — important for legal/compliance review.

Cross-case privilege firewall is critical for matters with multiple unrelated cases — bleed of one case's privileged content into another case's draft is a discovery nightmare. Requiring explicit `--include-case` opt-in + audit log makes cross-case retrieval a deliberate, traceable act.

Tier escalation (privileged-attached → local LLM mandatory) is the routing layer's hard-fail guarantee in action: privileged content never sees cloud.

## How (Approach)

1. **RAG retrieval** — `case-draft-helper.sh draft`:
   - Read `dossier.toon` for case context (parties, kind, status, recent timeline)
   - Read `sources.toon` for attached source IDs
   - Compose retrieval intent: `"<user-provided intent>; case kind: <kind>; parties: <parties>"` 
   - Call `knowledge-index-helper.sh query --intent "..." --scope case=<case-id>` (extension to t2850's CLI)
   - Retrieve top N=8 excerpts with anchors; cap total context size (8K tokens for short drafts, 32K for long)
2. **Tier resolution** — `_max_tier(sources)`: pick maximum sensitivity over all attached sources for the case. Use this as `--tier` to `llm-routing-helper.sh route`. If `privileged`, also force `--task draft` and let routing layer hard-fail if Ollama down.
3. **Prompt template** — `templates/case-draft-prompt.md`:
   ```
   You are drafting a {tone} {kind} for case {case-id} on behalf of {party-self}.
   The intent is: {intent}.
   Recent case timeline: {last 5 timeline entries}.
   Available evidence:
   {numbered list of excerpts with [source-id]: "excerpt..." anchors}
   
   Produce a draft that:
   - Cites every claim with [source-id] anchors
   - Stays {tone}; avoids speculation beyond the evidence
   - Length: {length}
   At the end, list "Drafted with reference to:" with each consulted source.
   ```
4. **Output writing** — write to `_cases/<case-id>/drafts/<timestamp>-<intent-slug>.md`:
   - Markdown with frontmatter: `case_id, intent, tone, length, model, generated_at, sources_consulted, cross_case_includes`
   - Body: the LLM output verbatim
   - Provenance footer (auto-appended even if model omits it): explicit list of source-ids with kind + sensitivity + sha
5. **Cross-case access** — `--include-case <id>`: validates `<id>` exists, appends audit entry to `_cases/<self-case-id>/comms/cross-case-access.jsonl` `{at, included_case, included_by, reason?}`, then queries that case's sources too
6. **Tone library** — `_config/draft-tones.json` defines tone presets (system-prompt fragments) so users can add custom tones per repo
7. **Revise mode** — `--revise <file> --feedback "..."`:
   - Read existing draft
   - Compose prompt: `"Revise this draft per feedback: {feedback}. Original draft: {body}"`
   - Same routing path; new file at `_cases/<case-id>/drafts/<timestamp>-<intent>-rev2.md`
8. **Tests** — covers happy path with mocked LLM, tier escalation when privileged-attached, cross-case access requires `--include-case` flag, provenance footer always present, revise mode preserves prior context

### Files Scope

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/case-draft-helper.sh`
- NEW: `.agents/templates/case-draft-prompt.md`
- NEW: `.agents/templates/draft-tones-config.json` (default `_config/draft-tones.json`)
- EDIT: `.agents/cli/aidevops` (add `case draft` subcommand)
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/knowledge-index-helper.sh` (add `--scope case=<id>` filter to `query`)
- NEW: `.agents/tests/test-case-draft.sh`
- EDIT: `.agents/aidevops/cases-plane.md` (drafting section + privilege firewall doc)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `aidevops case draft case-2026-0001-foo --intent "request payment of overdue invoice"` produces a draft file in `_cases/.../drafts/`
- [ ] Draft contains cited [source-id] anchors for every factual claim
- [ ] Provenance footer lists every source consulted with kind + sensitivity + sha
- [ ] Case with `privileged`-attached source: routing forces local LLM; draft fails if Ollama down
- [ ] Cross-case access without `--include-case`: only own case's sources appear in retrieval (verifiable via audit log)
- [ ] `--include-case <other-id>` flag: appends audit entry to `cross-case-access.jsonl`, includes other case's sources in retrieval
- [ ] `--tone formal` vs `--tone conciliatory`: visible difference in output style
- [ ] `--revise <file> --feedback "..."`: produces new revision file referencing prior draft
- [ ] `--dry-run` prints to stdout, does not write file
- [ ] Audit log records: case-id, intent, tone, model, sources consulted, tier, cross-case includes, generated_at
- [ ] No `auto-send` flag exists (drafts cannot trigger send)
- [ ] ShellCheck zero violations
- [ ] Tests pass: `bash .agents/tests/test-case-draft.sh`
- [ ] Documentation: drafting section in `.agents/aidevops/cases-plane.md`

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** t2851 (P4a — case dossier), t2852 (P4b — sources.toon, attach), t2850 (P1c — knowledge-index-helper query), t2847 (P0.5b — LLM routing), t2848 (P0.5c — Ollama for privileged)

- **Blocks:** post-MVP refinement; no MVP child blocked by this

## Worker Guidance


1. **Template format** — `_config/case-chase-templates/payment-reminder.eml.tmpl`:
   ```
   From: {{sender_email}}
   To: {{recipient_email}}
   Subject: Reminder: invoice {{invoice_number}} dated {{invoice_date}}
   
   Dear {{recipient_name}},
   
   This is a reminder that invoice {{invoice_number}} dated {{invoice_date}} for {{currency}} {{amount}} 
   remains outstanding. The original due date was {{due_date}}.
   
   Please advise on the status of this payment.
   
   Regards,
   {{sender_name}}
   ```
2. **Field resolution** — `case-chase-helper.sh _resolve_fields(case-id, template, recipient)`:
   - From dossier: `parties`, `kind`, `case_id`, `parties_self`, `parties_recipient`
   - From attached invoice (if any in `sources.toon` with `kind: invoice`): `invoice_number`, `invoice_date`, `due_date`, `amount`, `currency` (read from invoice's `extracted.json` from t2849)
   - From mailbox config: `sender_email`, `sender_name`
   - From `--to` flag or auto-detected recipient party email: `recipient_email`, `recipient_name`
   - Validate ALL fields resolved before substitution; missing field → exit 1 with explicit list
3. **Opt-in check** — read `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled`; if missing or false, exit 1 unless `--force` (which still requires `dossier.toon.chasers_enabled: false-with-force-allowed` — even more deliberate)
4. **SMTP send** — Python script `email_send.py` using stdlib `smtplib` + `email` module:
   - Connect to SMTP host (from `mailboxes.json` mailbox-id), STARTTLS
   - Auth with credentials from gopass
   - Compose `EmailMessage` from substituted template
   - Send, capture message-id
   - Return `{message_id, sent_at}` JSON
5. **Audit + timeline** — on success:
   - Append to `_cases/<case>/comms/sent.jsonl`: full record

   - Configurable retry: `case-chase-helper.sh retry <case-id> <message-id>` for manual retry
   - Two consecutive failures on same case: set case status to `hold` and fire alarm via t2853 via direct `case-alarm-helper.sh fire <case-id> --reason "chase send failure"`
7. **Template management** — `chase-template add|list|test`:
   - `add` opens editor on a fresh template, validates RFC 5322 + placeholder syntax
   - `test --case <case-id> --template <name>`: dry-run substitution, output to stdout (no send)

- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — single function modification with clear pattern to copy from `worktree-helper.sh:1196`

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-25
- **Session:** Claude Code interactive session
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (surfaced during t2859 investigation)
- **Parent task:** none (independent bug, not a child of t2840)
- **Conversation context:** While debugging t2859 (unbound `ORPHAN_WORKTREE_GRACE_SECS` causing 49 worktree destructions in 1h), inspected the SQLite worktree registry at `~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worktree-registry.db`. Found 815 April entries with stale PIDs — the cleanup pass deletes worktrees but never deregisters them from the ownership registry, so entries accumulate forever.

## What

`_cleanup_single_worktree` in `pulse-cleanup.sh` must call `unregister_worktree "$wt_path_age"` immediately after the worktree directory is destroyed (after `_trash_or_remove` succeeds). This mirrors the pattern already established in `worktree-helper.sh:1196` (the `cmd_remove` path).

After the fix:

- Pulse cleanup destroys a worktree → SQLite registry entry is removed in the same operation.
- `is_worktree_owned_by_others` cannot return false-positives for paths that no longer exist on disk.
- Registry size stays proportional to live worktrees, not lifetime cumulative.

## Why

The SQLite worktree registry (`worktree_owners` table) is the source of truth for `is_worktree_owned_by_others`, `check_worktree_owner`, and the conflict-detection that prevents two sessions from owning the same path. When pulse-cleanup destroys a worktree without deregistering it, the registry retains a row pointing to a path that no longer exists, with a PID that may have been long since recycled.

Concrete impact:

1. **Registry bloat:** 815 entries currently exist for ~7 live worktrees. The deployed registry contains entries dating from late March that should have been removed when the underlying worktrees were destroyed.
2. **PID-collision false positives:** if a stale entry's `owner_pid` happens to match a currently-running process (PIDs are reused), `check_worktree_owner` will report the path as actively owned even though it doesn't exist. The blast radius depends on how often PIDs collide on the user's machine — low probability per entry but probability rises with registry size.
3. **Diagnostic noise:** `prune_worktree_registry` (called only from `wt clean`, line 1921) is the only mechanism that removes stale entries, and it runs only on user invocation. Users who never run `wt clean` accumulate registry rot indefinitely.

`worktree-helper.sh::cmd_remove` already gets this right at line 1196 (`unregister_worktree "$path_to_remove"`). `pulse-cleanup.sh` is the divergent code path that needs to match.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Rationale:** Single-function edit in shell, but `pulse-cleanup.sh` is in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf` (dispatch-path file). Per build.txt §"Dispatch-Path Default (t2821)", dispatch-path tasks default to `no-auto-dispatch` + `#interactive` regardless of complexity. The fix itself is mechanical — copy a single line of pattern from a sibling file — but the file's blast radius (broken pulse cleanup → cascading worker damage like t2859) means this should land via maintainer review, not auto-dispatch.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task. PR body uses `Resolves #NNN` (where NNN is the GH issue number filed alongside this brief).

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh:459-463` — add `unregister_worktree` call after `_trash_or_remove` succeeds.

### Implementation Steps

1. Read the current cleanup block:

```bash
# Step 5b: perform removal (trash worktree dir + deregister + branch cleanup)
# ...
# Then deregister from git. Falls back to git worktree remove if trash fails.
_trash_or_remove "$wt_path_age" || git -C "$rp_age" worktree remove --force "$wt_path_age" 2>/dev/null || true
```

The comment claims "deregister from git" — but only the git-worktree-prune side is handled. The SQLite ownership registry is never touched.

2. Add the registry deregistration after the directory is destroyed. Model on `worktree-helper.sh:1196`:

```bash
# Source pattern at worktree-helper.sh:1196
unregister_worktree "$path_to_remove"
```

3. Apply to `pulse-cleanup.sh`. After the existing `_trash_or_remove` line (around line 462), add:

```bash
_trash_or_remove "$wt_path_age" || git -C "$rp_age" worktree remove --force "$wt_path_age" 2>/dev/null || true

# t2860: deregister from SQLite ownership registry to prevent stale entries.
# Mirrors the pattern in worktree-helper.sh:1196 (cmd_remove path).
unregister_worktree "$wt_path_age" 2>/dev/null || true
```

The `2>/dev/null || true` matches the existing tolerance — registry deregistration must never block cleanup.

4. Confirm `unregister_worktree` is in scope. `pulse-cleanup.sh` already sources `shared-constants.sh` which sources `shared-worktree-registry.sh`. If `command -v unregister_worktree` is empty in the cleanup context, source `shared-worktree-registry.sh` directly (mirror what `worktree-helper.sh` does).

5. Add a regression test at `.agents/scripts/test-pulse-cleanup-unregister.sh` modeled on `test-pulse-cleanup-config-defaults.sh` (just landed in t2859):
   - Create a temporary worktree in a sandbox repo
   - Register it via `register_worktree`
   - Trigger `_cleanup_single_worktree` (or its inner removal block)
   - Assert the SQLite entry is gone after cleanup completes

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** `_cleanup_single_worktree` in `.agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh`
- **Current line count:** approximately 60-80 lines (verify before editing)
- **Estimated growth:** +3 lines (one comment + one function call + one tolerance)
- **Projected post-change:** still well under 100-line function-complexity threshold
- **Action required:** None — well below threshold.

### Verification

```bash

# 2. Pattern verification
grep -n 'unregister_worktree' .agents/scripts/pulse-cleanup.sh
# Expected: at least one match in the _cleanup_single_worktree block

# 3. Behavioral test
.agents/scripts/test-pulse-cleanup-unregister.sh

# 4. End-to-end verification (after merge): live registry should stop growing
# Baseline: sqlite3 ~/.aidevops/.agent-workspace/worktree-registry.db "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM worktree_owners;"
# After 24h with cleanup running: count should be proportional to live worktrees, not cumulative.
```

- `.agents/scripts/test-pulse-cleanup-unregister.sh`

title: t2861: gh PATH shim mutates user --body-file source on disk instead of using a temp copy
body:
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn -->
# t2861: gh PATH shim mutates user --body-file source on disk instead of using a temp copy

## Pre-flight

- [x] Memory recall: "gh shim signature footer body-file" — 2 prior lessons confirm the shim has known parsing/race issues; this is a separate class
- [x] Discovery pass: no in-flight PRs touching `.agents/scripts/gh` in last 48h
- [x] File refs verified: `.agents/scripts/gh:327-335` checked at HEAD
- [x] Tier: `tier:standard` — single function modification with clear pattern, but `gh` shim affects every framework `gh` invocation

## Origin

- **Created:** 2026-04-25
- **Session:** Claude Code interactive session
- **Created by:** ai-interactive (surfaced during t2840 child-issue filing)
- **Parent task:** none (independent bug)
- **Conversation context:** During t2840 decomposition, called `gh issue create --body-file todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md` 16 times. After each call, the brief file on disk had been silently appended with a signature footer. The user-authored brief is the source of truth for the worker's implementation context — mutating it on every issue-creation call corrupts that source.

## What

The `gh` PATH shim must NOT modify the user's `--body-file` source on disk. When auto-injecting a signature footer, the shim must write the augmented body to a fresh temporary file and pass that temp path to the real `gh` binary, then clean up the temp file. The user's source file stays byte-identical before and after the call.

After the fix:

- `gh issue create --body-file todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md` does NOT modify `tNNN-brief.md`.
- A signature footer is still appended to the issue body that GitHub receives (functional contract preserved).
- Re-running the same command produces the same GitHub-side result without piling up signature blocks in the source file.

## Why

The current implementation at `.agents/scripts/gh:327-335` opens the user's source file in append mode and writes the signature footer directly into it:

```bash
if [[ $_body_file_idx -ge 0 && -n "$_body_file_val" && -f "$_body_file_val" ]]; then
    if ! grep -q "<!-- aidevops:sig -->" "$_body_file_val" 2>/dev/null; then
        _file_content=$(<"$_body_file_val") || _file_content=""
        _sig_footer=$("$SIG_HELPER" footer --body "$_file_content" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [[ -n "$_sig_footer" ]]; then
            printf '%s' "$_sig_footer" >>"$_body_file_val" || true
        fi
    fi
fi
```

This is a correctness bug for several reasons:

1. **Source-file mutation surprise.** A `gh issue create --body-file <foo>` call has the contractual semantics of "read foo, send to GitHub". The shim's append violates this contract — the file is also written to. Users editing the brief in their editor can lose changes if the file is open at the time (depending on editor behaviour around external modification).

2. **Signature pollution in version-controlled files.** Briefs at `todo/tasks/tNNN-brief.md` are committed. After a single `gh issue create` against a brief, the brief now has a signature footer that becomes part of the audit trail forever. The signature was meant for the issue body (machine-readable provenance for the GitHub surface), not the source brief.

3. **Idempotency illusion.** The current code guards against double-injection via `grep -q "<!-- aidevops:sig -->"`. That check protects against a second injection, but it does not undo the first. Once the marker is in the file, every subsequent call sees it and skips — but the file is already polluted. A user who re-runs the command after editing the brief gets stale signature data (wrong runtime, wrong session time, wrong token count) committed to the file.

4. **Mismatch with `--body` (string) handling.** The `--body` branch at line 312-323 modifies the in-memory args array without touching any file — exactly the right pattern. The `--body-file` branch should mirror this: write the augmented content to a new temp file and substitute the arg.

## Tier

**Selected tier:** `tier:standard`

**Rationale:** Single shim function modification with a clear local pattern (the `--body` branch immediately above is the model). Not in `.agents/configs/self-hosting-files.conf`, but the shim runs on every framework `gh` call — a regression here would silently corrupt issue/PR creation across all repos. Worth maintainer review rather than auto-dispatch.

## PR Conventions

Leaf task. PR body uses `Resolves #NNN`.

## How (Approach)

### Files to Modify

- `EDIT: .agents/scripts/gh:326-335` — replace the in-place file append with a temp-file substitution pattern.

### Implementation Steps

1. Replace the `--body-file` augmentation block. Current:

```bash
# --- --body-file case --------------------------------------------------------
if [[ $_body_file_idx -ge 0 && -n "$_body_file_val" && -f "$_body_file_val" ]]; then
    if ! grep -q "<!-- aidevops:sig -->" "$_body_file_val" 2>/dev/null; then
        _file_content=$(<"$_body_file_val") || _file_content=""
        _sig_footer=$("$SIG_HELPER" footer --body "$_file_content" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [[ -n "$_sig_footer" ]]; then
            printf '%s' "$_sig_footer" >>"$_body_file_val" || true
        fi
    fi
fi
```

Replace with a temp-file pattern:

```bash
# --- --body-file case --------------------------------------------------------
# t2861: write the augmented content to a fresh temp file rather than appending
# to the user's source. The user's brief on disk stays byte-identical.
if [[ $_body_file_idx -ge 0 && -n "$_body_file_val" && -f "$_body_file_val" ]]; then
    if ! grep -q "<!-- aidevops:sig -->" "$_body_file_val" 2>/dev/null; then
        _file_content=$(<"$_body_file_val") || _file_content=""
        _sig_footer=$("$SIG_HELPER" footer --body "$_file_content" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
        if [[ -n "$_sig_footer" ]]; then
            # Build augmented body in a temp file we own.
            _tmp_body_file=$(mktemp -t aidevops-gh-shim-body.XXXXXX) || _tmp_body_file=""
            if [[ -n "$_tmp_body_file" ]]; then
                printf '%s%s' "$_file_content" "$_sig_footer" >"$_tmp_body_file" || {
                    rm -f "$_tmp_body_file"
                    _tmp_body_file=""
                }
            fi
            if [[ -n "$_tmp_body_file" ]]; then
                # Substitute the arg pointing at user's file with our temp file.
                if [[ $_body_file_eq -eq 1 ]]; then
                    _modified_args[_body_file_idx]="--body-file=${_tmp_body_file}"
                else
                    _modified_args[_body_file_idx + 1]="$_tmp_body_file"
                fi
                # Schedule cleanup. exec clears traps, so register before exec
                # only — but exec replaces the process, so we cannot rm after.
                # Use a background reaper keyed on parent pid as a safety net.
                ( sleep 30 && rm -f "$_tmp_body_file" ) &
                disown
            fi
            # If temp creation failed, fall through silently — gh receives the
            # original file unmodified, the issue is created without a footer.
            # Better than corrupting the user's source.
        fi
    fi
fi
```

2. **Avoid the bash trap+exec problem.** The shim ends with `exec "$REAL_GH" "${_modified_args[@]}"`. `exec` replaces the process, so any `EXIT` trap registered earlier doesn't fire. The temp file would leak. Three options:

   - **Background reaper** (shown above): `( sleep 30 && rm -f "$_tmp_body_file" ) & disown`. Crude but reliable. 30s is more than enough for `gh` to finish reading the file.
   - **`mktemp` to `/tmp` directory and let the OS clean up at boot**: simpler, but litters `/tmp` until reboot.
   - **Replace `exec` with a normal call + `rm`**: changes process semantics — child becomes a real subprocess, exit codes still propagate but `gh`'s signal handling differs. Avoid unless the test suite specifically tests for parent-process behaviour.

   Recommend the background reaper.

3. Add a regression test `.agents/scripts/test-gh-shim-body-file-immutable.sh`:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regression test for t2861: gh shim must not mutate --body-file source.
set -euo pipefail

# Create a fixture brief
fixture=$(mktemp -t aidevops-test-brief.XXXXXX)
printf 'Test body\n\nSecond paragraph.\n' >"$fixture"
fixture_hash=$(shasum -a 256 "$fixture" | awk '{print $1}')

# Mock gh: just echo args, do not call the real binary
SHIM=~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/gh
REAL_GH=/bin/true SHIM_TEST_MODE=1 "$SHIM" issue create --body-file "$fixture" --title "test" 2>/dev/null || true

# Verify file is unchanged
fixture_hash_after=$(shasum -a 256 "$fixture" | awk '{print $1}')
if [[ "$fixture_hash" != "$fixture_hash_after" ]]; then
    echo "FAIL: --body-file source was mutated"
    diff <(printf 'Test body\n\nSecond paragraph.\n') "$fixture"
    rm -f "$fixture"
    exit 1
fi

rm -f "$fixture"
echo "PASS: --body-file source unchanged"
```

The test requires a `SHIM_TEST_MODE` env var that short-circuits the `exec` step (so the test can read the result of `_modified_args`). Add that minimal hook to the shim:

```bash
# At the top of the shim, near other early-return cases:
if [[ "${SHIM_TEST_MODE:-}" == "1" ]]; then
    # Test mode: print the resolved --body-file path and exit.
    # Used by test-gh-shim-body-file-immutable.sh.
    for ((_t = 0; _t < ${#_modified_args[@]}; _t++)); do
        case "${_modified_args[_t]}" in
        --body-file)
            printf 'resolved_body_file=%s\n' "${_modified_args[_t + 1]}"
            ;;
        --body-file=*)
            printf 'resolved_body_file=%s\n' "${_modified_args[_t]#--body-file=}"
            ;;
        esac
    done
    exit 0
fi
```

Insert this just before the final `exec "$REAL_GH" "${_modified_args[@]}"` line.

### Complexity Impact

- **Target function:** none (top-level shim script, not a function body)
- **Current line count:** 337 lines total in the shim
- **Estimated growth:** ~25 lines (replace existing 9-line block with ~25 lines + ~15 lines for SHIM_TEST_MODE branch)
- **Projected post-change:** ~360 lines total — still well under file-size threshold
- **Action required:** None.

### Verification

```bash
# 1. Lint
shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh

# 2. Regression test
chmod +x .agents/scripts/test-gh-shim-body-file-immutable.sh
.agents/scripts/test-gh-shim-body-file-immutable.sh
# Expected: PASS

# 3. End-to-end manual test
echo 'Test body' >/tmp/brief-test.md
hash_before=$(shasum -a 256 /tmp/brief-test.md | awk '{print $1}')
gh issue create --repo marcusquinn/aidevops-test --title "shim test" --body-file /tmp/brief-test.md --dry-run 2>&1 || true
hash_after=$(shasum -a 256 /tmp/brief-test.md | awk '{print $1}')
[[ "$hash_before" == "$hash_after" ]] && echo "PASS: file unchanged" || echo "FAIL: file mutated"
rm -f /tmp/brief-test.md

# 4. Verify temp files clean up after 30s
ls /tmp/aidevops-gh-shim-body.* 2>/dev/null
sleep 35
ls /tmp/aidevops-gh-shim-body.* 2>/dev/null && echo "FAIL: temp files leak" || echo "PASS: temp cleanup"
```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/gh`
- `.agents/scripts/test-gh-shim-body-file-immutable.sh`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `gh issue create --body-file <file>` does not modify `<file>` on disk.
- [ ] Issue body received by GitHub still includes the signature footer.
- [ ] `shellcheck .agents/scripts/gh` clean.
- [ ] New regression test `test-gh-shim-body-file-immutable.sh` PASSes.
- [ ] Temp files created by the shim are cleaned up within 60s of the gh call.
- [ ] `--body` (string) path remains unchanged — that branch is already correct.

## Context & Decisions

- **Why a temp file instead of converting `--body-file` to `--body`?** GitHub issue bodies have a 65k character limit but command-line argv has lower practical limits on some platforms. Briefs can be 500+ lines (~50k bytes) — converting to `--body` could hit argv limits. Temp file is the safer pattern.
- **Why a background reaper instead of in-process trap?** The shim ends with `exec`, which replaces the process and clears traps. Forking a sleep-then-rm and disowning it is the simplest reliable pattern for "delete this file in 30 seconds regardless of how I exit".
- **Why 30s sleep?** `gh` CLI typically completes a single issue create in 1-3s. 30s is 10x margin — long enough for slow networks, short enough that even a long-running `gh` operation has finished reading the file by then. (`gh` reads `--body-file` once at startup, not streaming.)
- **What about race conditions on the temp filename?** `mktemp -t` generates a unique filename; no race possible.
- **Why not also fix the `--body` branch?** It's already correct — it modifies the args array, not any file.

## Relevant Files

- `.agents/scripts/gh:312-323` — reference pattern: `--body` (string) branch handles augmentation in-memory without touching files.
- `.agents/scripts/gh:326-335` — current buggy `--body-file` handler.
- `.agents/scripts/gh-signature-helper.sh` — the helper that generates the footer; signature behaviour itself is unchanged.
- `prompts/build.txt` §"#8 Signature footer hallucination" — documents the signature contract this shim implements.
- Memory: WORKING_SOLUTION on parallel `gh issue create --body-file` race (2026-04-22T19:24:20Z) — separate bug class, will not be fixed by this task.

## Dependencies

- **Blocked by:** none
- **Blocks:** None directly. Reduces noise in committed brief files going forward.
- **External:** none

## Estimate Breakdown

| Phase | Time | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| Research/read | 10m | re-read .agents/scripts/gh:280-337 for full arg-parsing context |
| Implementation | 30m | replace block + add SHIM_TEST_MODE branch |
| Testing | 45m | write + verify regression test, manual e2e |
| **Total** | **~85m** | |

title: t2862: decouple pulse-merge into a fast standalone routine
body:
## Session Origin

Filed during interactive review of pipeline productivity gaps after merging t2842 (project validators). Observed: pulse cycles routinely take 5-10 minutes before reaching `deterministic_merge_pass` stage. In a 24h sample, merge pass ran only ~7 times despite ~40+ pulse cycles. Result: green PRs sit unmerged for 10+ minutes; manual `gh pr merge --admin` becomes the de-facto path for OWNER + `origin:interactive` PRs.

Evidence from `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse-stage-timings.log`:

```
2026-04-25T16:52:20Z deterministic_merge_pass 177  0  94659
(no merge pass entries for next 2.5 hours despite 8+ new pulse cycles)
```

Each cycle's preflight stack: `preflight_cleanup_and_ledger` (60-131s) + `preflight_capacity_and_labels` (~89s) + `preflight_early_dispatch` (~28s) + `complexity_scan` + ... = often 5+ min before merge pass even starts.

## What

Decouple `merge_ready_prs_all_repos()` from `pulse-wrapper.sh`'s monolithic cycle. Run it as an independent routine on a fast cadence (every 90-180s) so green PRs merge within ~3 min of CI completion regardless of preflight backlog.

## Why

Per `prompts/build.txt` "Mission" section: maximize ROI = maximize value per unit of time. Current state: PRs queued for auto-merge wait 10+ minutes for a slow pulse cycle to reach the merge stage. Manual workaround is `gh pr merge --admin --squash --delete-branch`, which works (per t2411) but should not be the primary path for `origin:interactive` + `OWNER` PRs.

Decoupling: doubling merge-pass frequency (from ~6/24h to ~14/24h) directly reduces "PR sitting green" time. Compound benefit on webapp where 8+ stuck PRs accumulated this session.

## How

### Files to modify

- NEW: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh` — standalone wrapper that sources `pulse-merge.sh` + dependencies, calls `merge_ready_prs_all_repos()`, exits cleanly. Mirror pattern: `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` (already standalone-invokable, sourced or executed).
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — keep the in-cycle merge call (defense-in-depth) but allow it to short-circuit if a merge routine ran within the last 60s (file timestamp marker). This avoids double-execution.
- EDIT: `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh` — initialize required env vars (`STOP_FLAG`, `REPOS_JSON`, `PULSE_MERGE_BATCH_LIMIT`) at the top of `merge_ready_prs_all_repos()` with `${VAR:-default}` form. Currently they assume `pulse-wrapper.sh` context — this BLOCKS standalone invocation. **Depends on t2863** (unbound-var sweep).
- NEW: `.agents/templates/launchd/sh.aidevops.pulse-merge-routine.plist` — launchd schedule for macOS, runs every 120s.
- EDIT: `setup.sh` — install the launchd plist alongside the main pulse plist.

### Reference pattern

Model on `.agents/scripts/pulse-dirty-pr-sweep.sh` — standalone-invokable AND callable as a function from pulse-wrapper. Has `--dry-run`, `--repo`, sourced-vs-executed detection, idempotency via state file. Reuse the exact shape.

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-routine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`
- `.agents/templates/launchd/sh.aidevops.pulse-merge-routine.plist`
- `setup.sh`

### Verification

title: t2863: sweep pulse-*.sh for set -u unbound variable bugs
body:
## Session Origin

Filed during interactive triage of pipeline productivity. Discovered while attempting to invoke `merge_ready_prs_all_repos()` standalone for a manual rescue pass: pulse-merge.sh and related pulse-*.sh scripts have multiple unbound-variable bugs that fire when context is missing. Same bug class as t2841 (`_b_nums` unbound in `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`), but more pervasive.

Specific instances observed in this session (all from `set -u` aborts):
- `pulse-merge.sh:547` → `STOP_FLAG: unbound variable`
- `pulse-merge.sh:552` → `REPOS_JSON: unbound variable`  
- `pulse-merge.sh:619` → `PULSE_MERGE_BATCH_LIMIT: unbound variable` (fires per repo iteration → flooded log with 14 lines)
- `pulse-issue-reconcile.sh:2007` → `_b_nums: unbound variable` (already fixed in t2841)

Each bug fires silently in production whenever the assumed context is absent, then aborts the function. Recurring evidence in `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` for months — see `_b_nums` history.

## What

Sweep all `pulse-*.sh` scripts for unguarded variable reads under `set -u`. Replace bare `$VAR` reads with `${VAR:-default}` form OR initialize at function top. Add a CI lint that detects the anti-pattern.

## Why

Per `prompts/build.txt` "Pre-implementation discovery" section: treat the codebase as a living system. Pulse cycles execute many code paths; any one path with `set -u` + unguarded read silently aborts a function. Symptoms: stages skip, recovery never fires, parent-tracker never closes (t2841 case), merge pass never runs (t2863 prereq for t2862).

The `_b_nums` bug fired 3-7 times per pulse cycle for hours/days before being caught. Sister bugs in pulse-merge.sh likely have similar production tenure. Sweep is preventive — saves debugging time on the next 5+ class-instances.

## How

### Files to modify

Discovery first:

```bash
# Find all "local VAR1 VAR2 VAR3" without inline init in pulse-*.sh
rg -n "^\s+local\s+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*(\s+[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*)+\s*$" ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh

# Find all bare $VAR refs that lack ${VAR:-} default in pulse-*.sh
# (heuristic — manual review of matches)
rg -n '"\$[A-Z_]{4,}"' ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-*.sh | rg -v '\$\{[A-Z_]+:'
```

Then triage matches:
- **Module-level state vars** (e.g. `STOP_FLAG`, `REPOS_JSON`, `LOGFILE`, `PULSE_MERGE_BATCH_LIMIT`): add a guarded init at function top:
  ```bash
  : "${STOP_FLAG:=/tmp/pulse-stop}"
  : "${REPOS_JSON:=$HOME/.config/aidevops/repos.json}"
  : "${PULSE_MERGE_BATCH_LIMIT:=10}"
  ```
- **Conditionally-assigned locals** (e.g. `_b_nums`): explicit init at declaration:
  ```bash
  local _g_nums="" _b_nums="" _p_nums="" child_nums=""
  ```
- **Truly required-from-caller vars**: assert and fail fast with mentor message:
  ```bash
  [[ -z "${REPOS_JSON:-}" ]] && { echo "ERROR: REPOS_JSON must be set" >&2; return 1; }
  ```

### Files Scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-conflict.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-feedback.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-issue-reconcile.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-core.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-engine.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-ancillary-dispatch.sh`
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` (caller — verify all required vars are exported when sourcing modules)
- NEW: `.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml` — diff-scoped lint catching new instances

### Reference pattern

Model the lint workflow on `.github/workflows/counter-stack-check.yml` (t2763 — counter-safety gate). Diff-scoped so pre-existing violations aren't blocked, only new ones.

The fix pattern is the t2841 commit (`e05bcae1f`) — identical shape applied across additional files.

### Verification

```bash
# Per-file: confirm function can be invoked without context
bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; source ~/.aidevops/agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh; type merge_ready_prs_all_repos'

# Confirm no new unbound errors in production after deploy
grep "unbound variable" ~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log | wc -l   # Should drop to ~0 over next 24h

# CI lint catches regressions
.github/workflows/pulse-unbound-var-check.yml on a synthetic PR with new "local x y z" line should fail
```

### Complexity Impact

This is a sweep — touches many files but each individual change is small (1-3 lines per affected function). No function should grow significantly. Total LOC delta ≈ +50 across ~7 files. The new CI workflow is ~80 lines (well under any function/file gate).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. All listed `pulse-*.sh` files pass `bash -n` AND `shellcheck` AND can have their public functions sourced+invoked without `unbound variable` aborts (function-level smoke test for top 5 entry points)
2. `~/.aidevops/logs/pulse.log` shows zero new `unbound variable` lines in the 24h after deploy (excluding pre-existing in scripts NOT in scope)
3. CI workflow `pulse-unbound-var-check.yml` exists and FAILS on a synthetic PR adding `local foo bar baz` (no init) to a `pulse-*.sh` file
4. Each fix is documented in commit message with the variable name and which path triggered it

### Non-scope

- Do NOT touch non-pulse scripts in this PR — separate sweep if needed
- Do NOT enforce on `local var` with single variable (those are usually fine; pattern of multi-var declaration is the high-risk case)
- Do NOT rewrite the affected functions for unrelated improvements — focused on var-init only
